dz.headline: algeria launches probe into food waste
dz.dek: videos show produce dumped outside cities to prevent price drops, prompting judicial action.
paragraphs: Algeria's judicial system is investigating the deliberate destruction of food, particularly tomatoes, to artificially keep prices high. The public prosecutor's office at the Court of Algiers ordered immediate and exhaustive inquiries on Thursday, October 22, following the circulation of videos on social media. These videos depict individuals discarding edible food and vegetables outside urban areas from trucks.

The investigations aim to identify all parties involved in these actions, including those who incited, financed, or profited from them, regardless of their position. The judicial authorities also seek to uncover the networks and distribution channels behind these practices. Those found guilty will face prosecution with the full force of current legislation.

This action follows President Abdelmadjid Tebboune's recent order to the Prime Minister to investigate fraudulent practices and speculation in the marketing of imported meats. The president had previously directed investigations into similar issues surrounding imported meat sales during a Council of Ministers meeting.

dz.headline: Algeria sets deadline for Mostaganem port specialization
dz.dek: Mostaganem port will exclusively handle public sector import operations starting January 1, 2027.
paragraphs: Algeria has set a timeline for the specialization of the Port of Mostaganem, designating it solely for public company import operations. The Port of Mostaganem company informed private economic operators that all non-public sector rolling traffic must be rerouted by October 31. A transition period until December 31 is available for ships with pre-scheduled rotations and existing commercial commitments.

Starting January 1, 2027, the port will no longer accept vessels not destined for public enterprises or organizations. The activity of self-entrepreneurs in maritime passenger transport is also being redirected to other ports by October 31. These measures are part of a national effort to reorganize port activities and transfer traffic to other locations.

This specialization is a component of Algeria's broader port modernization initiative aimed at reducing vessel waiting times and speeding up customs clearance and cargo unloading. The decision to reserve the port for public entities follows a directive from President Abdelmadjid Tebboune.

dz.headline: Algeria extends deadline for HR plan approvals
dz.dek: The General Directorate of Public Function and Administrative Reform has set November 10 as the final date for approving annual HR management plans for 2026.
paragraphs: The General Directorate of Public Function and Administrative Reform in Algeria has extended the deadline for approving annual human resources management plans for the 2026 fiscal year to November 10. This exceptional and final extension is due to delays in resolving legal reservations on some plans and new financial position data emerging in the fourth quarter of 2026.

In a dispatch dated October 18, 2026, the directorate informed ministry secretaries-general, governors, and heads of public function inspectorates of the new deadline. This decision follows an assessment of the progress in reviewing and approving these plans, which revealed outstanding legal reservations that require additional time for resolution to ensure proper HR management.

This measure follows a previous extension from March 15 to September 30, 2026. The current extension specifically covers the approval of plans already submitted within the initial deadlines and does not reopen submissions for new plans. The directorate stressed the exceptional nature of this final extension.

dz.headline: Algeria and Tunisia sign fisheries cooperation deal
dz.dek: Algerian and Tunisian fishing schools will exchange expertise and develop joint training programs.
paragraphs: Algeria and Tunisia have signed a framework agreement to enhance cooperation in fisheries, building on a long-standing tradition between fishermen from Algeria's El Kala and Tunisia's Tabarka. The deal, signed in Annaba, aims to exchange professional expertise in fishing techniques for "Dorade Coryphene" using fish aggregation devices.

The agreement was signed by Miloud Triaa, Director General of Fisheries and Aquaculture in Algeria's Ministry of Agriculture, and Ashraf Ben Soliman, Director General of the Tunisian Professional Group for Fisheries Products. Triaa stated the accord will strengthen bilateral cooperation and develop partnerships between specialized training institutions to improve professional skills and joint practical training.

The workshop concluded with recommendations for a joint project at Algeria's National Center for Research and Development in Fisheries and Aquaculture, in coordination with Tunisia's National Institute of Marine Sciences and Technologies. This project will involve practical field trips and testing of fish aggregation devices to advance "Dorade Coryphene" fishing techniques and knowledge.

ao.headline: Angola leads SADC satellite committee
ao.dek: Zolana João chairs the 16-nation Shared Satellite Steering Committee for Southern Africa.
paragraphs: Angola is leading a Southern African Development Community (SADC) initiative to develop a jointly owned satellite, with engineer Zolana João presiding over the Shared Satellite Steering Committee. This project aims to leverage satellite infrastructure for connectivity, Earth observation, and economic development across 16 member states.

João, who also leads Angola's GGPEN, is working to convert satellite technology into practical tools. Initiatives like the ANGEO-1, Angola's first high-performance Earth observation satellite, are designed to support environmental monitoring, disaster response, and national development planning. The Angola Geodata Center (GEDAE) is integral to transforming this data into decision-making support.

The ambition is to extend connectivity to rural areas through projects like ANGOSAT-2 and Connecta Angola, while Earth observation applications will aid agricultural planning and climate change response. João, affiliated with MIT, is also involved in a NASA-funded drought response system for Angola and participates in international discussions on space governance and Africa's role in the space economy.

bj.headline: Benin Beach Tour hosts 23 teams in Cotonou
bj.dek: The second stage of the 2026 Benin Beach Tour will feature 11 women's and 12 men's teams competing from October 23 to 25.
paragraphs: The Benin Beach Tour (BBT) is organizing its second stage of the 2026 edition from October 23 to 25 on Erevan beach in Cotonou. 23 teams, including 11 women's and 12 men's formations, will compete over three days. This competition is an important passage towards the season's grand finale.

Soulé Arouna, the deputy national technical director for beach volleyball, explained the project's philosophy to the press on Wednesday, October 21, at the Benin Volleyball Federation headquarters. The BBT aims to provide regular competition and establish a ranking system to track team performance. The federation, supported by its president Ali Yaro, is backing this initiative.

The Benin Volleyball Federation secretary general, Cokou Romain Ahlinvi, stated the goal is to gain international recognition for the BBT and enable athletes to participate in ranking competitions. Foreign teams may participate pending necessary approvals. The event includes a technical meeting on Friday, matches starting Saturday, and finals on Sunday.

bj.headline: Benin ranks 94th in 2026 rule of law index
bj.dek: The country's overall score improved slightly, with gains in civil justice but a decline in freedoms.
paragraphs: Benin placed 94th out of 143 countries in the World Justice Project's 2026 Rule of Law Index, released on October 21. The nation's overall score reached 0.47 out of 1, a less than 1% increase from the previous year. Benin ranked 10th among 34 sub-Saharan African nations evaluated.

The country achieved its highest global rank of 79th for constraints on government powers, fundamental rights, and criminal justice. Benin was ranked 89th for regulatory enforcement, 91st for order and security, and 92nd for absence of corruption. However, civil justice and open government were its least favorable areas, at 108th and 115th globally.

The WJP report noted improvements in access to and affordability of civil justice, alongside a lack of discrimination in this area. Conversely, freedom of opinion, expression, assembly, and association declined. These results contrast with the regional trend where 23 of 34 evaluated countries saw their scores decrease over the past year.

bj.headline: Benin handball team appoints French coach
bj.dek: Euphémie Dartron-Lairy will lead the senior women's national team for the 2026 CAN tournament.
paragraphs: Euphémie Dartron-Lairy, a French coach of Guadeloupean origin, has been appointed technical coordinator for Benin's senior women's handball team. She will lead the team, known as the Amazons, in the 2026 Women's Senior CAN tournament scheduled for December 2-12 in Tunisia. Dartron-Lairy aims to develop Benin's women's handball by focusing on human connection, team cohesion, and performance.

Dartron-Lairy, trained by the French Handball Federation, describes herself as a "facilitator of potential." Her career includes coaching and management roles, notably with ASUP men's team where they won 13 titles in 16 competitions and were French National 3 runners-up in 2022. She moved to mainland France in 2021 to further her coaching development and has been coaching Palente Besançon Handball in the second division since July 2025.

Beyond the sport, Dartron-Lairy sees her role with the Benin selection as a personal project. As someone of African descent, she stated her motivation extends beyond handball itself. Her experience includes developing young talent and coaching at various levels in France and Guadeloupe.

bj.headline: Benin proposes electric buses for commuters
bj.dek: The government is considering a new public transport system to reduce travel costs for citizens.
paragraphs: Millions of Beninese citizens face high daily travel expenses due to the lack of a structured public transport system. The current informal sector, relying on motorcycles and modified minibuses, has led to increased road accidents and pollution. President WADAGNI's government is exploring a political choice to implement a new public transport solution.

The proposal focuses on a network of electric buses, starting with the densely populated corridor between Cotonou and Abomey-Calavi. This initiative aims to provide a more affordable and efficient mobility option, drawing lessons from successful public transport models in Dakar and Abidjan. These cities demonstrate that state support is essential for public transport viability.

The government views subsidizing public transport as a social investment, treating mobility as a right rather than a privilege. This move acknowledges the economic reality that public transport systems, like those in Paris and London, often require partial state funding to operate effectively and offer economies of scale.

bw.headline: Botswana eyes 25% De Beers stake as luxury firms bid
bw.dek: Global luxury giants and diamond industry players are pursuing majority control of the struggling miner.
paragraphs: Botswana is positioning itself to acquire a 25 percent stake in De Beers as global luxury investors prepare to take control of the struggling diamond producer. The proposed ownership structure could see private investors collectively controlling 51 percent of De Beers, with Botswana, Namibia, and Angola sharing the remaining 49 percent.

The Global Diamond Consortium (GDC), led by former De Beers CEO Gareth Penny, is the preferred bidder for Anglo American’s 85 percent shareholding. Bloomberg reported that Botswana and GDC are nearing an agreement to increase the government's existing 15 percent stake to approximately 25 percent, making Botswana the largest individual government shareholder.

Swiss luxury conglomerate Richemont, owner of Cartier and Van Cleef & Arpels, is in advanced discussions to join the Penny-led consortium. Individual stakes for Namibia and Angola remain undisclosed, and the allocation of shares among private investors has yet to be finalized.

bw.headline: Botswana to host regional trading for Dangote refinery IPO
bw.dek: The Botswana Stock Exchange will act as a regional hub for investors seeking access to the US$1.6 billion refinery share offering.
paragraphs: The Botswana Stock Exchange (BSE) will serve as the regional trading hub for the US$1.6 billion Dangote Petroleum Refinery initial public offering (IPO). This arrangement, coordinated by the Committee of SADC Stock Exchanges (CoSSE), aims to simplify investor access to the Nigerian refinery's shares.

CoSSE chairman Collen Tapfumaneyi announced last Wednesday in Gaborone that regional exchanges will concentrate trading through Botswana, allowing investors to use domestic brokers. Access Bank Botswana will issue Botswana Depository Receipts, each representing one Dangote Refinery share, facilitating an offering of up to US$500 million with trading expected to start on 14 December 2026.

This move follows a Reuters investigation highlighting regulatory hurdles and restricted distribution channels for foreign investors in the original Nigerian IPO prospectus. Concentrating trading via Botswana could improve liquidity and retain local brokerage activity, although participating markets must still meet their own regulatory requirements.

bw.headline: Botswana proposes P60 billion to restore public assets
bw.dek: A proposed five-year programme aims to repair schools, roads, and water systems built with diamond wealth.
paragraphs: Botswana is considering a P60 billion programme to restore public assets built with diamond wealth. The proposed "Restoration Botswana" initiative would focus on repairing existing infrastructure like schools, hospitals, roads, and water systems before commissioning new projects. This plan aims to ensure the nation's mineral inheritance translates into lasting prosperity through functional public services.

The programme suggests an annual allocation of P12 billion over five years, with potential budget scenarios ranging from P40 billion to P90 billion. This initiative addresses the issue of deferred maintenance, which can turn inexpensive repairs into costly rehabilitation projects and lead to premature asset replacement. The current development to asset management spending ratio of 7:1 is seen as a risk to the nation's built assets.

The 2026/27 budget allocated P1.85 billion for maintaining and rehabilitating public assets, falling short of the estimated P10 billion needed annually. A sector-by-sector analysis suggests approximately P7 billion is required to bring public schools to minimum acceptable standards. The proposal advocates for asset management to claim 50% of the development spending envelope, shifting resources from new construction to preserving existing services.
bw.body:
Botswana is considering a P60 billion programme to restore public assets built with diamond wealth. The proposed "Restoration Botswana" initiative would focus on repairing existing infrastructure like schools, hospitals, roads, and water systems before commissioning new projects. This plan aims to ensure the nation's mineral inheritance translates into lasting prosperity through functional public services.

The programme suggests an annual allocation of P12 billion over five years, with potential budget scenarios ranging from P40 billion to P90 billion. This initiative addresses the issue of deferred maintenance, which can turn inexpensive repairs into costly rehabilitation projects and lead to premature asset replacement. The current development to asset management spending ratio of 7:1 is seen as a risk to the nation's built assets.

The 2026/27 budget allocated P1.85 billion for maintaining and rehabilitating public assets, falling short of the estimated P10 billion needed annually. A sector-by-sector analysis suggests approximately P7 billion is required to bring public schools to minimum acceptable standards. The proposal advocates for asset management to claim 50% of the development spending envelope, shifting resources from new construction to preserving existing services.
bw.why: Botswana's public infrastructure, including schools and water systems, faces deterioration due to deferred maintenance, impacting the services they provide.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso, Turkey agree to boost education cooperation
bf.dek: Ankara talks between the two nations also covered increased scholarships for Burkinabe students.
paragraphs: Burkina Faso and Turkey held political consultations in Ankara on October 20-21, 2026, to strengthen cooperation. The Burkinabe delegation, led by Ambassador Hermann Yirigouin TOE, met with Turkish officials from various state structures, including the Maarif Foundation, TIKA, the Council of Higher Education, and the Ministry of Health.

Discussions with the Maarif Foundation focused on signing an agreement for school establishment and management, as the foundation already operates schools in Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso. The foundation agreed to increase scholarships for Burkinabe students and provide support for vocational and technical training.

TIKA, the Turkish development agency, committed to supporting Burkina Faso in vocational and technical training in 2027 and is considering opening an office in Ouagadougou. The Council of Higher Education also agreed to renew an academic cooperation accord and increase Master's and Doctorate scholarships for Burkinabe students.

bf.headline: Lomé port seeks stronger ties with Burkina Faso traders
bf.dek: Port officials met Ouagadougou business leaders on October 23, 2026, to discuss trade facilitation.
paragraphs: Officials from the Port of Lomé and the Alliance for the Promotion of the Port of Lomé (A2PL) met with Burkinabè economic operators in Ouagadougou on Friday, October 23, 2026. The meeting aimed to strengthen collaboration and ease the transit of goods to Burkina Faso. This event was part of a promotional mission from October 18 to 24, 2026, focused on improving trade with the Alliance of Sahel States.

During the session at the Burkinabè Shippers' Council, Lomé port representatives presented their services and addressed concerns from Burkinabè businesses. Awèmèwètou Haladoko, secretary general of A2PL, highlighted the port's performance, noting that in 2025 it handled nearly 36 million tonnes of cargo and processed about 2.5 million 20-foot equivalent containers. The average waiting time for container ships at anchor was reduced to 21 hours and 39 minutes.

The port also detailed its specialized handling capacities for strategic products, including 100 to 117 tonnes per hour for wheat and over 350 tonnes per hour for clinker. Efforts to streamline administrative procedures through digitalization, such as the One-Stop Shop for International Trade Formalities (GUFORD), were also discussed. A Task Force AES 2026 was established to address challenges faced by economic operators.

bf.headline: IB Bank staff donate blood in Ouagadougou
bf.dek: The bank's staff mutual organised a blood drive to support health facilities facing high demand.
paragraphs: The staff mutual of IB Bank Burkina organised a blood donation drive on Friday at the bank's headquarters in Ouagadougou. The operation, in collaboration with the National Blood Transfusion Centre (CNTS), aimed to increase the supply of blood products for health facilities. This initiative mobilises bank workers for a gesture of solidarity to help those needing transfusions.

Moïse Kafando, a member of the mutual's bureau, stated that the organisation wants to contribute to public health and the population's well-being. He explained that blood donation was chosen to launch the mutual's activities due to the importance of health. Marguétou Derra/Mané, head of collection at the Ouagadougou blood transfusion centre, praised the initiative, noting high demand from maternity, pediatric, and security forces units.

Derra/Mané highlighted that blood is a precious resource not available through ordinary drug sales and urged the public to engage in voluntary donation. She stressed that meeting transfusion needs is a collective responsibility. The IB Bank staff mutual aims to promote mutual aid and civic responsibility, encouraging other companies to support public health actions.

bf.headline: Anselme Traoré defends thesis on profit crime in Burkina Faso
bf.dek: Anselme Traoré was admitted with highest honors for his research on profit crime from 1987 to 2015.
paragraphs: Anselme Traoré successfully defended his doctoral thesis on profit crime in Burkina Faso between 1987 and 2015 at the Norbert Zongo University in Koudougou on Friday. He was awarded the highest honors for his work, which was examined by a jury led by Professor Salifou Idani.

Professor Idani noted that Traoré's analysis of societal components offered relevant solutions for authorities. Traoré stated his research shows a rise in profit-related offenses, some escalating from street crime to organized crime, driven by a risk-reward assessment. He suggested reducing contributing factors is key to combating these crimes.

Zara Dao, Traoré's thesis director, praised his contribution to Burkina Faso's economic and social history, highlighting the under-researched topic of profit crime. The jury also included Professor Mahamadou Oubda, with Master of Conferences Soualiouno Méité Ben from Ivory Coast and Research Master Wenceslas Sourbar Justin Hien serving as rapporteurs.

Ganamé, who began his IT career at Burkina Faso's Office National des Télécommunications in 1999, holds a doctorate in computer security from the University of Franche-Comté in France. His expertise combines scientific research with entrepreneurship to create protective digital solutions.

bi.headline: Burundi demolishes market stalls, traders fear ruin
bi.dek: Ruyigi officials say stall demolitions prevent fires, but small business owners face lost income and debt.
paragraphs: Small traders in Burundi's Ruyigi market face ruin after authorities began demolishing their kiosks and selling points on September 16. The communal administration in Buhumuza province claims the operation aims to prevent fires and clear access for firefighters. Affected vendors, including palm oil, food, and fruit sellers, fear losing their primary income and being unable to repay loans taken for their businesses.

Traders reported having official authorization for their stalls and expressed surprise at the demolitions, stating they had recently spent capital on school expenses and restocking. Many had taken loans from local banks. They worry that relocation outside the market will reduce customers and income. Communal administrator Diane Niyibitanga stated the decision was made with trader representatives, citing fire risks and the need for clear access routes for emergency services, adding that traders were informed three months prior.

Niyibitanga warned that opposition to the demolitions could lead to sanctions, including reimbursement of demolition costs, administrative fines, or legal action. Local police are prepared to support the operation. The demolitions are impacting vendors of palm oil, cotton, food products, fruits, vegetables, and tailors using irons.

bi.headline: Burundi PARCEM accuses government of restricting fertilizer imports
bi.dek: The watchdog group fears new rules will favour a few privileged importers over fair market competition.
paragraphs: The Burundian organization PARCEM has denounced new government rules for importing chemical fertilizers, announced on October 21. PARCEM's national director, Faustin Ndikumana, stated that the measures could replace the current monopoly with a system favouring a select group of privileged importers, harming competition and investment. The Ministry of Environment, Agriculture, and Livestock outlined conditions including a letter to the ministry detailing the type, quantity, and origin of desired fertilizers, such as DAP and urea.

Ndikumana expressed concern on October 22 that the new system would not guarantee a genuine market opening, potentially perpetuating existing issues. Farmers in Gitega province are already reporting a lack of FOMI fertilizers for the current growing season, raising fears of reduced harvests and increased food insecurity. PARCEM questions the selection criteria, such as land size, and suggests experienced economic operators should also be allowed to import.

PARCEM warns that such a system could discourage investors and encourage corruption, advocating for transparent and objective import criteria accessible to all capable operators. Across Burundi, farmers report not receiving ordered fertilizers despite prior payments, with some alleging selective distribution favouring ruling party militants and associated traders. The ministry also extended the payment deadline for existing fertilizer stock until October 24, with distribution set to begin on October 26.

bi.headline: Burundi marks 33rd anniversary of president Ndadaye assassination
bi.dek: A sober commemoration took place in Bujumbura on October 21, 2026, for the first democratically elected president.
paragraphs: Burundi observed the 33rd anniversary of the assassination of President Melchior Ndadaye and his collaborators on October 21, 2026. The commemoration occurred at the Place des martyrs de la démocratie in Bujumbura, with significant military and security presence. Attendees, including the president's widow, were searched upon entering the perimeter around the former 'Palais du 1er Novembre'.

The ceremony honored President Ndadaye, who was democratically elected, and the unknown martyr, with a red carpet laid to their tombs. Among the attendees were the widow of former president Pierre Nkurunziza, former president Sylvestre Ntibantunganya, the governor of Bujumbura, and the administrator of Mukaza. Government representation included the Minister of the Interior and the government's spokesperson.

High-ranking officials, including the President of the Senate and the President of the National Assembly, also attended the event. The President of the Republic arrived later, greeted by military and police officials lining the red carpet. This date marks 33 years since the 1993 assassination and subsequent large-scale killings.

bi.headline: Burundi official buried without autopsy amid death questions
bi.dek: Bruce Sebanza, an official at the Burundi Development Agency, died October 13, with family alleging torture.
paragraphs: Bruce Sebanza, an official at the Burundi Development Agency (ADB), died on October 13, 2026, at the institution's premises in Bujumbura. He was buried on Wednesday, October 21, without a public autopsy, prompting questions from observers. The National Independent Human Rights Commission (CNIDH) visited the ADB and requested investigations into the circumstances of his death.

At a service in Bujumbura, Sebanza's mother described his death as "barbaric torture." Relatives reported that Sebanza's body was transported to the Kamenge military hospital in a government pick-up truck on October 13. They stated the body was unclothed, wearing a soiled, bloodied singlet and underwear, with visible abrasions on his cheeks.

Witnesses reported hearing distress calls from the ADB premises during the night of October 12 to 13. A morgue worker allegedly mentioned physical marks on the body consistent with constriction, possibly by a rope. No independent medical conclusions on the cause of death have been released.

cm.headline: Cameroon targets CFA1.12 trillion for farm investment
cm.dek: The AgriConnect pact aims to cut food imports by 28% and boost production of corn, palm oil, rice, milk, and fish by 2030.
paragraphs: Cameroon launched the AgriConnect pact in Yaoundé on October 21, 2026, to attract investment into eight agricultural sectors. The initiative requires nearly CFA1.12 trillion ($1.87 billion) for 24 interventions planned between 2026 and 2030. The goal is to reduce the country's food import bill by 28% by 2030, from approximately $1.6 billion to $1.15 billion.

The pact, supported by the World Bank Group and the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), aims to increase domestic production and develop local food processing. It focuses on corn, rice, cassava, palm oil, cocoa, soybeans, milk, and fisheries. By 2030, Cameroon aims for 6 million tons of corn and 800,000 tons of palm oil annually, with domestic rice covering 55% of demand and milk meeting 60% of consumption.

IFAD and the World Bank are partners in the action framework designed to accelerate sector transformation and strengthen food security. The program also seeks to create jobs, particularly for young people and women, and mobilize public and private investment.

cm.dek: Combined profits fell to CFA15 billion in 2025 despite a 5.9% revenue increase to CFA82.6 billion.
paragraphs: Globeleq's two power plants in Cameroon reported combined profits of CFA15 billion in 2025, a 24.2% decrease from CFA19.8 billion the previous year.

Despite the profit drop, total revenue for the plants rose 5.9% to CFA82.6 billion in 2025, up from CFA78 billion in 2024. The Kribi gas plant saw profits fall by more than half to CFA6 billion, while Dibamba's thermal plant profit rose to nearly CFA9 billion.
Both plants continue to face cash flow issues, with unpaid electricity bills causing some generating units to go offline and reducing cash distributions.

cm.headline: Cameroon power line loses 44.7% of electricity
cm.dek: The Logbaba–Bassa 1 transmission line in Douala lost nearly nine times the acceptable electricity threshold in November 2025.
paragraphs: Cameroon's Electricity Sector Regulatory Agency (ARSEL) recorded a 44.7% active power loss rate on the 90-kilovolt Logbaba–Bassa 1 transmission line in Douala in November 2025. This amounted to 22,326 megawatt-hours (MWh) of lost electricity, far exceeding the regulator's 5% acceptable technical threshold.

ARSEL has recommended audits to investigate the high losses on the 4.131-kilometer line, suggesting potential issues with infrastructure or measurement accuracy. In May 2025, the same line had already reported 10,258 MWh in losses, a 14.7% loss rate.

Other transmission lines also show significant losses, with the Garoua–Guider line experiencing rates between 8.2% and 18.9% over six months. The National Electricity Transmission Company (Sonatrel) published an infrastructure inventory for the affected line in March 2025.

cm.headline: Cameroon nears 80% completion of anti-money laundering plan
cm.dek: The nation has completed 19 of 24 actions to exit GAFI's enhanced surveillance and restore investor trust.
paragraphs: Cameroon has completed 19 of 24 actions to combat money laundering and terrorism financing, raising its implementation rate from 46% to nearly 80%. The nation aims to finalize the remaining five measures to exit enhanced surveillance by the Financial Action Task Force (GAFI). This progress was reported at a meeting in Yaoundé on October 22, 2026, chaired by Minister Delegate Yaouba Abdoulaye.

The economic and reputational stakes are high, as being on GAFI's grey list increases financing costs and slows financial flows. To exit this list, administrations must complete the final actions and reinforce controls in the non-financial sector.

This acceleration of reforms is intended to secure the national financial system and enhance the country's attractiveness to economic partners. The government seeks to reassure investors and improve the country's financial reputation.

cm.headline: Citibank executive Ella Martin chairs AmCham Cameroon
cm.dek: The American Chamber of Commerce in Cameroon appointed Ella Martin, a Citibank executive, as its new board chair.
paragraphs: Citibank executive Ella Martin has been appointed the new board chair of the American Chamber of Commerce in Cameroon (AmCham Cameroon). She succeeds Laure E. Djoukam, head of Shekina Invest, who will continue as a director on the board. The chamber's new leadership team also includes Leah Malla Rackovsky as vice chair and Émilie Siewe as treasurer, with expertise in banking and financial technology.

The board features seven additional directors, including Hélène Dengoue, Richard Fowang, Laure E. Djoukam, Sarada Nya, Alain Nono, John Phipps, and Salamatou Bantse. These directors represent companies involved in sectors such as oil and gas, telecommunications, consumer goods, and legal services. AmCham stated its new leadership will focus on enhancing trade and investment between Cameroon and the United States.

The organization aims to improve services for its member companies. Rackovsky, founder of Azamra Financial Technologies, previously led AmCham's Emerging Technologies Committee. Siewe will now oversee the chamber's financial operations.

cf.headline: Central African Republic denies border violation
cf.dek: The presidency stated that recent military operations against rebels occurred solely within its territory.
paragraphs: Central African Republic's presidency has affirmed that recent military operations involving its FACA forces and Russian allies took place exclusively within the nation's borders. Presidential spokesperson Albert Yaloké Mokpeme stated at a press conference in Bangui that there are no tensions with neighboring Chad, and the two heads of state communicate regularly to secure their shared border. He clarified that the operation against rebel leader Noureddine Adam, supported by Chadian and Sudanese mercenaries, occurred entirely on Central African soil without violating Chadian territory.

Mokpeme explained that the FACA and their allies acted to neutralize armed groups preparing a large-scale attack in the tri-border area of the Central African Republic, Chad, and Sudan. He reported that the clashes resulted in casualties on both sides, with some attackers fleeing into Chad. The spokesperson warned that any attempt to use neighboring countries as bases to destabilize the Central African Republic will be met with severe force by the FACA and their allies.

The presidency's statement aims to prevent any frontal country from serving as a rear base for negative forces seeking to destabilize Central African institutions. The FACA and their allies intervened effectively, leading to exchanges of fire that caused injuries on both sides.

cf.headline: Central African Republic civil society leaders arrested
cf.dek: Organisations pleaded with President Touadéra for the release of five leaders detained after an October 12 protest.
paragraphs: Five civil society leaders remain detained in the Central African Republic following their arrest after an October 12 "dead city" day protest. Organisations met President Faustin-Archange Touadéra on October 21 to advocate for their release. The protest was organised to object to rising fuel prices.

The Minister of Interior, Bienvenu Zokoué, has invoked the events of 2013, suggesting that current mobilisations against fuel price hikes threaten the nation's stability. This statement follows the arrests of five civil society leaders in Bangui.

President Touadéra responded to the organisations by citing the principle of the separation of powers. The detained leaders were arrested after the October 12 demonstration against increased fuel costs.

cf.headline: CAR advisor accuses France, Chad of plot
cf.dek: Jules Njawé claims 103 armed vehicles and French fighter jets are preparing an attack on the Central African Republic.
paragraphs: Jules Njawé, an advisor to Central African Republic President Faustin-Archange Touadéra, accused Chad and France on October 19, 2026, of plotting an attack against the country. Njawé claimed 103 heavily armed pick-up trucks, Sudanese fighters, and two French fighter jets were involved in the alleged offensive, seeking to divert attention from recent clashes.

These accusations follow an October 10 military operation in the Vakaga region where Russian Wagner group mercenaries reportedly attacked Front Populaire pour la Renaissance de la Centrafrique positions in Nabagaye-Tissi. During this operation, 16 Chadian soldiers were wounded on their own territory, according to reports.
The initial report from Corbeau News Centrafrique stated 14 wounded soldiers, later updated to 16 by October 13. Njawé made his claims during an October 19 broadcast hosted by Alain Foka.

km.headline: Comoros police trained in crime scene management
km.dek: 20 officers completed a week-long course on preserving evidence and coordinating interventions.
paragraphs: 20 Comorian security agents, including 10 police officers and 10 gendarmes, completed a week-long training on crime scene management. The course, held at the Ministry of Interior, concluded on Friday, October 23, 2026, focusing on securing locations and preserving evidence.

The training was organized by the security service of the French Embassy in collaboration with the Comorian Ministry of Interior. Participants practiced methods for securing crime scenes and preserving evidence to aid investigations, aiming to improve coordination between the police and gendarmerie.

Upon completion, the 20 agents received certificates recognizing their acquired knowledge. The training emphasized applying these new skills to enhance citizen security through improved daily interventions.

km.headline: Comorian man found dead on Marseille highway
km.dek: The family of Kassim, known as Mkataba on TikTok, confirmed his death on October 23.
paragraphs: The family of Kassim, known on TikTok as Mkataba, confirmed his death on Friday, October 23, 2026. The Comorian man, in his thirties and living in Marseille, had been missing since October 16. His body was reportedly found on the A7 highway in Marseille.

The exact circumstances of his death and how he came to be on the highway remain unclear. Questions linger about the timeline between his disappearance and the announcement of his death, whether this delay relates to the discovery of his body, its identification, or informing the family. Mkataba had reportedly received death threats on TikTok due to disputes, but no link to his death has been established.
The precise details surrounding his demise are still under investigation.

cg.headline: Congo hosts regional trade talks for women
cg.dek: Brazzaville conference aims to boost women's participation in central African commerce.
paragraphs: Brazzaville is hosting a regional conference from October 21 to discuss how to increase women's involvement in trade across central Africa. The meeting, themed "Unlocking the Economic Potential of Central African Women to Accelerate the Inclusive Implementation of AfCFTA," brings together ministers, regional bodies, and entrepreneurs.

The conference seeks to identify ways for women entrepreneurs and traders to benefit more from the African market. Participants are working to create a regional roadmap to improve women's access to markets and cross-border trade, addressing challenges like access to finance and support systems.

This initiative aims to make the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) an instrument for economic inclusion and opportunity. The three-day event in the Congolese capital focuses on strengthening women's roles in regional economic integration.

He led an official delegation to discuss the promotion and protection of human rights across Africa.

Minister Bininga stated that while the Republic of Congo has made progress in human rights, continuous efforts are necessary. He emphasized that effective human rights protection requires constant commitment from public authorities and all stakeholders.

ci.headline: Dabou prefect calls for collective action against illegal gold mining
ci.dek: Prefect Michèle Hortense Amani Loboué urged community leaders and residents to join the fight against illegal gold mining.
paragraphs: Dabou prefect Michèle Hortense Amani Loboué called for collective action to combat illegal gold mining in the department on October 22, 2026. The prefect stated that the illegal activity is causing significant water pollution, forest destruction, and land degradation. This illegal mining also disrupts local economies, threatens social cohesion, and results in lost state revenue.

Mme Amani Loboué emphasized that prefectural authorities and security forces alone cannot win the fight against illegal gold mining. She specifically requested the engagement of village chiefs, community leaders, landowners, officials, guides, youth, and women. The prefect encouraged sub-prefects of Dabou, Lopou, and Toupah to continue awareness campaigns in their areas.

Discussions during the meeting covered the legal framework for artisanal mining, environmental impacts, and ways to strengthen trust between security forces and the public. While Dabou has no reported cases of illegal gold mining, the department of Grand Lahou does. The prefect urged constant vigilance and reporting of suspicious activities to authorities to preserve the department and ensure sustainable development.

ci.headline: Ivory Coast court postpones Tidjane Thiam PDCI leadership hearing
ci.dek: A court in Abidjan adjourned a case challenging Tidjane Thiam's election as PDCI president until November 19.
paragraphs: A court in Abidjan postponed a hearing on Tidjane Thiam's election as president of the Democratic Party of Ivory Coast (PDCI). The hearing was adjourned until November 19 after the judge decided to consolidate additional legal actions.

Two party members brought the case claiming the party's rules were not followed during the electoral process. These include a challenge by another member seeking to annul resolutions from last year's party congress and appoint an interim president. The first two suits are against the PDCI, while a third case targets Thiam and his vice president directly.
In May 2025, an Ivorian court dismissed a previous legal challenge against Thiam's leadership of the PDCI, which argued he was ineligible due to acquiring French citizenship in 1987.

ci.headline: Ivory Coast opposition proposes new election authority
ci.dek: Opposition parties want an independent body to manage polls, excluding political representatives.
paragraphs: Opposition parties and movements in Ivory Coast are advocating for a reformed electoral governance structure, proposing the creation of an independent National Electoral Authority (AENI). This new body would be responsible for organizing elections and referendums, aiming to strengthen the credibility of polls by operating on principles of independence, neutrality, impartiality, transparency, and professionalism.

The proposed mechanism includes a complementary structure, the Permanent Election Observatory (OPE), tasked with monitoring the electoral process, evaluating its regularity, and issuing alerts and recommendations. A National Selection Committee (CNS) would also be established to recruit members for both bodies, without direct involvement in the practical organization of the votes. The AENI would be an autonomous public institution with administrative, financial, technical, and operational independence.

The AENI's mandate would cover the entire electoral cycle, from voter list establishment and revision to the proclamation of provisional results. Its leadership would be a college of 11 members from diverse professional backgrounds, excluding political party and government representatives. The OPE would independently observe and evaluate, with its recommendations reviewed by the AENI, which must provide reasoned responses and publish a follow-up report.

eg.headline: Egyptian pound hits historic low against US dollar
eg.dek: The Egyptian pound closed at 55.35 per dollar on Thursday, a record drop against the US currency.
paragraphs: The Egyptian pound reached a historic low against the US dollar on Thursday, closing at 55.35 pounds per dollar in commercial bank trading. This rate surpassed the previous record of 54.75 pounds set in April. The dollar’s selling rate reached 55.37 pounds at Al Baraka Bank, and between 55.33 and 55.35 pounds at other major Egyptian banks.

Central Bank of Egypt Governor Hassan Abdalla stated that the exchange rate moves dynamically with economic conditions and that fluctuations are normal. He urged the public not to worry about currency movements, emphasizing the banking system's resilience. Abdalla explained that a fixed exchange rate would be more concerning than a flexible one amid changing circumstances.

The pound has depreciated by approximately 13.8 percent against the dollar since February 27, when the official rate was around 47.72 pounds per dollar. The dollar’s buying and selling rates rose by between 0.90 and 0.92 pounds across five banks on Thursday.

The meeting occurred on the sidelines of Quad mechanism discussions with three European nations. Both ministers agreed to coordinate actions to support security and stability in Libya.

eg.headline: Egypt health minister cites spending gains
eg.dek: Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar highlighted 16 presidential initiatives benefiting 95 million citizens with LE44 billion.
paragraphs: Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar stated on Tuesday that Egypt's leadership support for the healthcare sector is unprecedented. He spoke at the Egypt Forum 2026, recalling a significant disease burden and inadequate budgets in 2014. The minister said state development plans have improved the sector, pointing to 16 presidential initiatives that cost LE44 billion and reached 95 million citizens.

Abdel Ghaffar stressed that healthcare success is measured by citizen experience, not just spending. However, government data shows a decline in public hospital beds from 98,291 in 2013 to 84,225 in 2024, while private beds increased. The total number of hospital beds nationwide decreased from 124,300 in 2013 to 120,239 in 2024.

Egypt has not met the constitutional mandate of allocating at least three percent of GNP to public healthcare since 2014, with spending rarely exceeding 1.7 percent. For the current fiscal year, the government allocated 1.51 percent of GNP. A new calculation method, including off-budget entities like police and military hospitals, is now used to claim the minimum spending threshold is met.

eg.headline: Israeli forces arrest cancer patient and daughter returning to Gaza
eg.dek: Amal Ghazy al-Rify and her daughter were detained at Karam Abu Salem checkpoint after two years of medical treatment in Egypt.
paragraphs: Israeli forces arrested a cancer patient, Amal Ghazy al-Rify, and her daughter Yasmin Rifaat al-Rify on Tuesday evening as they returned to Gaza from Egypt. The two women had been in Egypt for nearly two years seeking medical treatment for Amal's cancer. They were detained at the Karam Abu Salem checkpoint after passing through the Rafah crossing, which had reopened that day.

A relative, Haitham al-Rify, stated that Amal's health had deteriorated, prompting their decision to return to Gaza despite incomplete treatment. He condemned their arrest, emphasizing that neither woman is involved in political or military activities. The family has not been informed of their whereabouts and has contacted the International Committee of the Red Cross for details.

The family appealed on Wednesday for urgent intervention from human rights organizations to uncover the fate of Amal and Yasmine and secure their release. 29 patients and 42 companions had left Gaza on Tuesday for treatment in Egypt, including critical and chronic disease cases.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea updates 2006 textbooks
gq.dek: A commission of over 90 sub-commissions will review and update educational materials to reflect the country's changes.
paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea's Ministry of Education is updating and reprinting teaching manuals last revised in 2006. Vice President Nguema Obiang Mangue presided over a meeting in Malabo where Minister of State Clemente Engonga Nguema Onguene explained the project's progress. A technical working commission with more than 90 sub-commissions is reviewing the books to correct errors and update content, incorporating teacher feedback.

The updated manuals will reflect changes in Equatorial Guinea over the past 20 years, including information on municipalities, urban districts, history, culture, and traditions. The Vice President authorized the editorial representatives to work with ministry technicians on revisions. He also instructed the Prime Minister to ensure other implicated ministries submit pending information to prevent further delays.

Two workshops will be held in Malabo and Bata to analyze commission reports and consolidate observations into a single document for the publisher. The goal is to ensure the new textbooks accurately represent the country's evolution.

paragraphs: The president of Equatorial Guinea's Supreme Court of Justice, Francisco Evuy Nguema, has denounced the arbitrary application of judicial rulings within the country's penal system. He cited the case of Gregorio Mesian Nseme Ada, known as Goyo, whose judicial orders were disregarded at Black Beach prison. This situation illustrates how powerful individuals can override legal decisions.

Evuy Nguema stated that judicial sentences and release orders can become meaningless when they conflict with the will of those in power. The case of Goyo is presented as a severe example of this arbitrariness, revealing the vulnerability of the system when its own mechanisms are undermined. The report suggests this signals a potential unraveling of authority.

The denunciation by the Supreme Court president indicates a fracture within the country's power structures. The report implies that such disregard for legal processes by those in authority exposes their own weaknesses. This event highlights a struggle between judicial independence and executive power in Equatorial Guinea.

er.headline: US lifts sanctions on Eritrea
er.dek: Sanctions removed on September 19, 2026, targeted the ruling party's financial and military apparatus.
paragraphs: The United States removed sanctions on Eritrea on September 19, 2026. These sanctions were imposed in 2021 due to Eritrea’s involvement in the Tigray War. The US government had outlined plans to lift the sanctions four months prior, according to a Reuters report.

Human rights groups criticized the decision, citing Eritrea's record of forced labor and torture under the ruling People’s Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ). Eritrea's government called the sanctions 'illicit and immoral' and claimed they caused 'incalculable damage' and constrained development.

The removed sanctions targeted the PFDJ’s financial and military bodies and two officials, Abraha Kassa and Hagos Gebrehiwet. The Eritrean Defence Force’s chief of staff, Filipos Woldeyohannes, remains under separate sanctions. The PFDJ has previously benefited from the removal of UN sanctions in 2018, remaining self-sufficient.

paragraphs: A woman was pulled from the rubble of a 16-storey building that collapsed in Nairobi's Eastleigh area on Friday afternoon. Rescue operations are ongoing as emergency teams search for seven people feared trapped beneath the debris. The building's underground construction collapsed, causing panic in the clothing district.

Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud stated that rescue efforts are complicated by reports of a second person heard crying for help, whose cries have since gone silent. The building had not been cleared for occupation, raising questions about why investors allowed it to be occupied. The number of casualties remains unconfirmed.

Authorities are expected to investigate the building's structural condition and compliance with safety requirements. The immediate priority is the search for survivors and providing medical assistance to those rescued. Further updates are expected as teams establish the full impact of the collapse.

ke.headline: Kenya records second Ebola death

paragraphs: Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola, a 65-year-old woman who was a close family member of the country's first patient. The Ministry of Health confirmed the death on Friday evening, bringing the total fatalities to two among nine confirmed cases.

The woman developed symptoms on October 13 while under quarantine and was admitted to an infectious disease unit the same day. She received supportive care but died early Friday. Health officials are working with her family on a safe burial. Seven patients remain under treatment in isolation facilities.

All nine confirmed cases are linked to a single cluster of known contacts, and the ministry stated there is currently no evidence of community transmission. Authorities urged the public to avoid contact with bodily fluids of sick people and to practice regular handwashing.

ke.dek: Kenyan farmers and exporters can now sell dried chillies to China after meeting strict quality and safety rules.
paragraphs: Kenyan farmers, processors, and traders will now export dried chillies to China, a major consumer market. The Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Service (KEPHIS) announced this market access on October 16, 2026.

KEPHIS stated that this development allows Kenyan producers to diversify export markets and increase trade. Exporters must register their facilities with China's General Administration of Customs (GACC) through KEPHIS and meet stringent phytosanitary and food safety requirements.
All farmers, drying facilities, and packhouses must also register with KEPHIS. Each shipment to China requires a KEPHIS Phytosanitary Certificate to confirm compliance with the set standards.

za.headline: three cops convicted over nathaniel julies murder
za.dek: Constable Caylene Whiteboy fired the fatal shot, while two other officers planted evidence.
paragraphs: Three police officers have been convicted in the Gauteng Division of the High Court in Palm Ridge for the August 2020 murder of 16-year-old Nathaniel Julies in Eldorado Park, Johannesburg. Constable Caylene Whiteboy was found guilty of murder and defeating the ends of justice for firing the fatal shot. Sergeant Simon Ndyalvane was convicted of murder, unlawful possession of ammunition, defeating the ends of justice, and perjury. Detective Voster Netshiongolo was found guilty of unlawful possession of ammunition and perjury but acquitted of being an accessory after the fact.

The court heard that Whiteboy claimed she believed her firearm was loaded with rubber bullets when she shot Julies, who had Down syndrome, after he left his home for a tuckshop during Covid-19 lockdown. Evidence presented by the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) revealed that Netshiongolo, with Ndyalvane's assistance, planted ammunition and fabricated a story that Julies was caught in a crossfire. Julies was pronounced dead at Chris Hani Baragwanath Hospital.

The officers remain on bail pending pre-sentencing proceedings scheduled for November 11. NPA regional spokesperson Magaboke Mohlatlole stated that the convictions represent an important step towards accountability and reaffirm that no one is above the law. The NPA hopes the conclusion of the trial will provide some measure of closure for the Julies family.

za.headline: South Africa court halts illegal weight-loss jab production
za.dek: Regulators won a legal battle against a pharmacy compounding popular weight-loss drugs, but illegal sales continue.
paragraphs: South African regulators have won a court case against iDexis, a Tshwane pharmacy illegally compounding weight-loss injections like Ozempic. The Gauteng High Court ordered the pharmacy to stop producing semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic, after large quantities of its compounded drugs were seized. This action follows a surge in demand for weight-loss jabs, which suppress appetite and prolong feelings of fullness.

Stavros Nicolaou, chairperson of the Pharmaceutical Task Group, stated on October 14 that while the court order is a victory, regulators like Sahpra and the South African Pharmacy Council need to act swiftly with clearer guidelines. He warned that momentum could be lost if action is not taken quickly, leaving consumers at risk from illegal and experimental drugs. The panel included representatives from Sahpra, the police, and border control to address the trade in fake medicines.

Sahpra has received approximately 600 complaints this financial year regarding illegitimate and fake medicines sold through informal channels, including online, gyms, and hairdressers. Australia has already banned similar pharmacy compounding of weight-loss jabs, deeming them potentially unsafe. New rules to combat this trade in South Africa are still months away, leaving enforcement gaps.

za.headline: Kaizer Chiefs lose CAF Confederation Cup tie on penalties
za.dek: Amakhosi won the match 1-0 against Red Arrows but could not convert three penalties in the shootout.
paragraphs: Kaizer Chiefs have been eliminated from the CAF Confederation Cup after a 3-2 penalty shootout loss to Red Arrows. The Soweto giants won the second leg match 1-0, with Bradley Cross scoring a header in the 66th minute to level the aggregate score at 1-1. However, the team failed to convert three of their five penalties during the shootout, resulting in their exit.

Coach Fernando da Cruz made several changes to the team that lost the previous week, including starting Bruce Bvuma in goal and bringing back Lebohang Maboe. The attack was led by Wandile Duba, Pule Mmodi, and Mduduzi Shabalala, who struggled to convert crosses into goals. Shabalala missed two clear chances to win the tie for Chiefs before the penalty shootout.

The starting XI for Kaizer Chiefs included Bvuma, Frosler, Cross, Miguel, Moloisane, Mthethwa, Mabaso, Mmodi, Duba, Shabalala, and Abrahams. The team opted to play wide, delivering crosses into the box that found no effective finishing. Despite winning the match 1-0, the penalty shootout determined their progression to the group stage.

ng.headline: Nigeria confirms imported Ebola case in Abuja
ng.dek: A woman with recent travel history to Uganda tested positive for Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease on October 20.
paragraphs: Nigeria confirmed an imported case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in Abuja on October 20, 2026. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare announced the case after laboratory testing identified the virus in a woman who had recently traveled from Uganda. She developed symptoms on October 7 and sought care at a private facility on October 11.

The patient has been isolated and is receiving medical care, while health officials investigate the infection's source and trace her movements. 44 contacts have been identified and are being monitored. This confirmation on the 12th anniversary of Nigeria being declared Ebola-free by the WHO raises questions about the nation's preparedness for a resurgence of the virus.

The 2014 Ebola outbreak in Nigeria resulted in 20 cases and eight deaths before containment. The World Health Organisation declared Nigeria Ebola-free on October 20, 2014, after 42 days without new cases. Swiss authorities have denied claims that the current patient visited the Democratic Republic of the Congo before falling ill.

ng.headline: Butcher stabs colleague to death in Ogun over sweeping chore
ng.dek: Police arrested Selim Ayodele, 21, after a disagreement with Ibrahim Wasiu, 26, at their workplace on Sunday, October 18, 2026.
paragraphs: Ogun State Police have arrested 21-year-old butcher Selim Ayodele for allegedly stabbing his 26-year-old colleague, Ibrahim Wasiu, to death. The fatal incident occurred on Sunday, October 18, 2026, after work at their cow meat-selling outlet in Alagbole, Ogun State. A disagreement over who should sweep the floor led to the altercation.

Police Public Relations Officer DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi stated that the Ajuwon Police Station received the report at 8 p.m. Ayodele allegedly stabbed Wasiu in the chest and twisted the knife. Wasiu was confirmed dead on arrival at Life Hospital and his body was taken to Life Channel Private Mortuary pending an autopsy.

The suspect, Ayodele, is in custody as investigations continue for prosecution. Commissioner of Police Bode Ojajuni urged residents to resolve disputes peacefully and report criminal incidents. The command stressed the importance of avoiding violence over minor disagreements.

ng.headline: Veteran Nollywood actor Francis Duru dies at 57
ng.dek: President Bola Tinubu and Nollywood practitioners mourn the passing of the versatile performer, known for his role in 'Rattlesnake'.
paragraphs: Veteran Nollywood actor and filmmaker Francis Duru has died at the age of 57. His family announced his passing on Friday, October 23, 2026, following a brief illness. Duru was a recognisable face in the Nigerian film industry, with a career spanning several decades.

President Bola Tinubu expressed deep sorrow over the death, calling it a painful loss to Nollywood and Nigeria’s creative community. Colleagues, including actors Kanayo Kanayo and Kate Henshaw, paid tribute to Duru’s versatility and contributions. The Actors Guild of Nigeria also mourned the loss of the "great thespian."

Duru studied Theatre Arts at the University of Port Harcourt and was known for his role as Ahanna in the 1995 film 'Rattlesnake'. He also featured in other productions such as 'Sound and Rhythm of Love' and 'Blood Money'. He was also regarded as a mentor to emerging talents.

ng.headline: Nigeria plans framework for farmer climate finance
ng.dek: A new system aims to guide investments for adaptation and resilience against drought and flooding.
paragraphs: Nigeria is developing a framework to improve access to climate finance for small-scale farmers, guiding investments in agricultural adaptation and protecting rural livelihoods. The initiative will provide financial institutions with clear guidelines for supporting farming activities resilient to climate challenges like drought and flooding. This framework was discussed at a validation workshop in Abuja organised by the Presidential Implementation Committee on Technology Transfer (PICTT) and YAPU Solutions.

PICTT Chairman Dahiru Muhammed stated the framework aims to translate Nigeria’s national climate taxonomy into a practical system for accessing and channeling funds. He explained that while the Federal Ministry of Finance and the UN Development Programme developed the taxonomy, PICTT and partners are establishing implementation mechanisms for rural communities. Muhammed stressed that defining eligible climate adaptation activities is essential for farmers and agricultural enterprises to benefit from financing.

Country Representative of WorldFish in Nigeria, Charles Nyangbe, noted the need for financing solutions tailored to varying regional environmental conditions, such as drought in the north and flooding in the south. YAPU Solutions Managing Director Christoph Junghleisch estimated smallholder farmers could need up to $30 billion annually to respond to climate risks, describing climate adaptation as a significant investment opportunity.

gh.headline: Ghana needs 759 million cedis for health supply chain
gh.dek: The government plans to use domestic resources to fund a four-year master plan amid withdrawal of foreign aid.
paragraphs: Ghana requires over 759 million cedis to address critical gaps in medicine and medical supplies for its health facilities over the next four years. The government is seeking domestic funding for the 2025-2029 health sector supply chain master plan as some foreign aid to the health sector is being withdrawn. This plan aims to ensure health facilities, especially those serving women and children, have essential commodities.

The new master plan is a revision of the 2021-2025 plan, which achieved 35% of its targets due to COVID-19. The revised plan includes 47 strategic interventions across two technical areas to ensure availability, timely access, and affordability of quality health commodities. Dr. Edward Bright Agyekum, Director for Procurement and Supply Chain at the Ministry of Health, stated that local resource mobilization is key, with strategies in place to achieve priorities despite potential donor withdrawal.

The master plan seeks to build an integrated distribution system for medical stores and develop a well-coordinated financial system for the public health sector by 2029. It also includes a mapping exercise to track money flow and expenditures. Daniel Oswald Owusu Afranie, Technical Director with the Global Health Supply Chain, emphasized the need for the country to own the implementation for universal health coverage by 2030.

gh.dek: Former MP Sarah Adwoa Safo announced her decision to contest the NPP parliamentary primaries after consultations with party leaders.
paragraphs: Former Dome-Kwabenya Member of Parliament Sarah Adwoa Safo has declared her intention to run in the New Patriotic Party (NPP) parliamentary primaries for the constituency. This reverses her earlier stated plans to seek opportunities elsewhere. Her decision, announced on Thursday, October 22, 2026, follows discussions with NPP leadership and executives.

Adwoa Safo, who served as the MP for Dome-Kwabenya for 12 years, stated her commitment to the constituency's development. She aims to build on past achievements and address ongoing challenges. The former MP highlighted the NPP's improved vote count in the constituency from 63,373 in 2012 to 75,041 in 2020 under her representation.

She is now calling for engagement with party members, stakeholders, and constituents as she seeks to represent Dome-Kwabenya again in Parliament. Adwoa Safo previously announced she would not contest the seat.

gh.headline: Absa Place earns IFC EDGE Advanced green building certification
gh.dek: The new Accra headquarters of Absa Bank Ghana Ltd achieved the certification for energy and water efficiency.
paragraphs: Absa Bank Ghana Ltd’s new headquarters, Absa Place, has earned EDGE Advanced certification from the International Finance Corporation (IFC). The building, located at 64 Independence Avenue, Ridge, Accra, was recognised for its high standards in energy and water efficiency. The IFC’s EDGE Advanced system assesses improvements in energy use, water consumption, and the embodied carbon of construction materials.

The certification affirms the bank’s commitment to developing infrastructure that delivers long-term operational efficiency, according to Absa Bank Ghana Ltd Managing Director Dr Edward Nartey Botchway. IFC’s Principal Country Officer for Ghana, Deo Onyango, stated that the achievement demonstrates how sustainability can contribute to competitiveness and long-term value creation.

Absa Place features a 570-kilowatt-peak solar installation designed to meet at least 80 per cent of the bank’s on-site electricity needs. The building also uses a water-cooled chiller system and a glass façade that blocks over 70 per cent of external heat. In 2025, the bank operated 54 solar-powered ATMs generating approximately one million kilowatt-hours of clean energy annually.

cd.headline: DR Congo finance inspection plans 2026-2028 strategy
cd.dek: Academics and experts in Kinshasa reviewed a three-year plan for systemic financial control and digitalization.
paragraphs: The Inspection Générale des Finances (IGF) in the Democratic Republic of Congo is modernizing public finance control with its 2026-2028 strategic plan. From October 21 to 22, 2026, academics and scientists met in Kinshasa to discuss the plan's focus on systemic control, risk prevention, and digital procedures. This reform aims to integrate university and scientific communities into the IGF's work.

At the Pullman Grand Hotel, professors, researchers, and experts debated the shift from traditional compliance checks to a systemic, preventive, and digital approach. IGF Inspector General Christophe Bitasimwa Bahii stated the institution will use data analysis and risk mapping to anticipate irregularities. Participants noted challenges like poor digital infrastructure, limited electricity, and funding for research.

Discussions also covered public sector ethics, agent responsibility, and performance evaluation for transparency. Contributions came from academics like Ekolo Adiaka and Claude Sumata Motukula, and officials including Olga Kavira Kinyamusiti. Examples from Estonia, Denmark, Rwanda, and Kenya were cited for their digital governance benefits.

cd.headline: DR Congo's SNEL seeks debt restructuring with six banks
cd.dek: The state-owned electricity company aims to finance four new projects through international financial institutions.
paragraphs: The Société nationale d’électricité (SNEL) is discussing debt restructuring and financing for four electricity projects with six international banks. SNEL's Director General, Teddy Lwamba, met with representatives from JPMorgan, HSBC, Standard Chartered, Absa Group, Dubai Islamic Bank, and EXIM Bank of India on October 22, 2026, in Dubai. These discussions occurred on the sidelines of the Invest Africa forum.

SNEL currently dedicates 60% of its revenue to repaying commercial and financial debts, leaving only 15% for operations, maintenance, and investments. The company also faces challenges collecting payments from public institutions, which owe approximately 23.07 million USD for 2025, with only 3.88% of the expected 24 million USD paid. This situation highlights SNEL's financial fragility due to high debt servicing and poor revenue collection.

Financial analysts suggest that debt restructuring could improve SNEL's cash flow through rescheduled payments. However, they caution that new investments require better collection rates, sustainable pricing, and careful resource management. The outcome of the Dubai discussions will depend on the agreements reached and their ability to increase electricity generation and transport capacity.

cd.headline: DR Congo assembly passes referendum law
cd.dek: Parliamentary opposition boycotted the vote, calling it a forceful move that could harm national dialogue.
paragraphs: The National Assembly in the Democratic Republic of Congo adopted a law on organizing a referendum on Friday, October 23. The assembly considered reservations from the Constitutional Court before passing the text, which now returns to the Senate for a second review. The bill will then go to the president for promulgation.

The parliamentary opposition boycotted the debate and passage of the law, denouncing what they called a forceful move. Christian Mwando, head of the opposition group Ensemble pour la République, warned that passing the law without opposition participation would shut down dialogue. He stated the majority would bear responsibility for the law, which he claimed would be solely backed by the Union sacrée.

Majority deputies praised the law's adoption as a sign of democratic function and majority rule, asserting the opposition's absence did not halt proceedings. President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi had previously sent the law back to parliament for reconsideration after the Constitutional Court raised concerns.

cd.headline: DR Congo plans 370km road upgrade with Arab Contractors
cd.dek: Prime Minister Judith Suminwa met with Arab Contractors Sub-Sahara to discuss the Ilebo-Kananga route modernization project.
paragraphs: Prime Minister Judith Suminwa met with a delegation from Arab Contractors Sub-Sahara on October 22, 2026, in Kinshasa to discuss the construction and modernization of the 370-kilometer Ilebo-Kananga road. This strategic route aims to improve access to the Kasaï region, facilitating the transport of goods and agricultural products. The project also includes the construction of four bridges.

Hassan Mohamed Hassoun, regional director for Arab Contractors, stated that the company and its financial partners, including Trade and Development Bank (TDB) and United Bank for Africa (UBA), have submitted their offer. The road is intended to boost economic development by improving trade with Kinshasa and supporting agricultural activities. Arab Contractors plans to support local agricultural cooperatives, particularly those led by women.

The company hopes to begin construction in early 2027, pending administrative procedures, which could take two to three months to finalize. This infrastructure development aligns with the government's 2024-2028 action plan priorities for transport, territorial access, and agricultural support.

tz.headline: Tanzania aims for top 10 global food producer status
tz.dek: Prime Minister Nchemba announced the goal at the Borlaug Dialogue in Des Moines, USA, citing Vision 2050.
paragraphs: Prime Minister Mwigulu Nchemba stated Tanzania's ambition to join the world's top 10 food-producing nations by 2050. This goal is part of Tanzania’s Development Vision 2050, aiming for leadership in African food production. Nchemba announced this during the Norman Borlaug International Dialogue in Des Moines, United States.

Tanzania has achieved a 130 per cent food self-sufficiency level through its agricultural initiatives. Agricultural exports increased from US$2.1bn in 2021/2022 to US$3.7bn in 2024/2025. Agriculture contributes 24.6 per cent to Tanzania’s GDP and employs 65 per cent of the workforce.

Nchemba urged increased investment in farmers, science, youth, women, and resilient food systems to support Africa's agricultural potential. He stressed the need for action and innovation to build food systems for present and future generations, under the theme 'Before Hunger Defeats Us'.

tz.headline: Tanzania expands health insurance to all income groups
tz.dek: The government launched the second phase of its Universal Health Insurance scheme, aiming to cover all citizens regardless of their ability to pay.
paragraphs: Tanzania's Health Minister Mohamed Mchengerwa launched the second registration phase of the Universal Health Insurance scheme in Mtwara on October 23, 2026. This expansion opens enrolment to all income groups, including those who can finance their own membership, moving beyond the initial focus on the poorest households. The initiative aims to ensure that a person's ability to pay does not prevent them from seeking necessary medical treatment.

Health Permanent Secretary Dr Grace Magembe stated that the scheme is now open to everyone, encompassing both those who can afford their own cover and those classified by the government as unable to pay. Mtwara was chosen for the national launch due to its leading performance in the first phase's enrolment. The Universal Health Insurance Act, 2023, makes insurance compulsory and mandates employer registration for workers in formal and informal employment.

The first phase, which began on January 26, 2026, targeted 276,004 households identified as unable to afford insurance, with the government allocating Sh48.8 billion. While 997,015 beneficiaries were registered, only 495,034 had collected membership cards, highlighting the need for the second phase to ensure usable cover. The Ministry of Health's 2026/27 budget statement indicates phase two will also register an additional 589,772 households unable to pay.

tz.headline: Muhas trains 27 health workers in dialysis
tz.dek: The five-week hemodialysis training at Muhas aimed to improve kidney patient care across Tanzania.
paragraphs: Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences (MUHAS) in Dar es Salaam has completed its fifth hemodialysis training for 27 health professionals. The participants, including doctors, clinical officers, and nurses, underwent the short course which began on September 14, 2026, and concluded on October 23, 2026. This training is part of MUHAS's efforts to enhance the skills of healthcare providers in treating patients with kidney failure.

Meshack Shimwela, Registrar of Private Health Facilities, stated that the training is an important step in improving healthcare services and patient efficiency, noting that Tanzania now has 77 hemodialysis centers, with 29 government-owned. Professor Emmy Meta, MUHAS Director of Continuing Education, reported that 105 health professionals have been trained across various regions since the program's inception, with this latest cohort including two doctors, 17 clinical officers, and eight nurses from Dar es Salaam, Arusha, Morogoro, and Kagera.

The training involved classroom theory, practical skills in MUHAS's lab, and five weeks of clinical practice. Practical sessions took place at Muhimbili National Hospital and five Africa Healthcare Network (AHN) dialysis centers in Dar es Salaam. These centers include Shree Hindu Mandal Hospital, Cardinal Rugambwa Hospital, CCBRT, E.M. Hospital, and Shree Hindu Mandal Super Specialized Polyclinic. Professor Meta emphasized the importance of follow-up to assess the practical application of learned skills.

tz.headline: Tanzania minister orders review of Mbeya transport routes
tz.dek: Bajaji drivers and vendors resume work after a four-day protest over market and route changes in Mbeya.
paragraphs: Bajaji drivers and vendors in Mbeya, Tanzania, returned to work on October 23 after a four-day protest that disrupted transport and trade. The stoppage ended following a directive from Prof Riziki Shemdoe, the Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, ordering a 14-day review of bajaji and daladala routes and access to a planned market. The review will involve drivers, traders, the Mbeya City Council, LATRA, and the Regional Commissioner’s Office.

The dispute began on October 12 when Mbeya Regional Commissioner Jumanne Sagini ordered the City Council to allocate formal spaces for traders and bajaji operators within seven days. The council planned to direct bajaji outside the TANZAM highway and relocate 1,715 traders to Old Airport, Kabwe, and Mwanjelwa. Enforcement on October 19 led to drivers being forced to clear areas and vendors having goods seized, prompting the joint protest.

Erica Mlembe, a vendor at Kabwe, stated on October 19 that her goods were seized and she had no place to work, impacting her ability to pay school fees. The conflict also affected daladala services, with bajaji drivers attacking them with stones from October 19, leading to increased transport fees and people walking on October 20. The 14-day review is the latest documented outcome as of October 23.
