tz.headline: Tanzanian opposition figure charged with treason
tz.dek: John Pambalu faces potential death penalty for alleged election obstruction and protests.
paragraphs: John Pambalu, a senior official with Tanzania's Chadema party, was charged with treason on Wednesday, a crime carrying a potential death penalty. The charges stem from alleged actions intended to obstruct the October 2025 General Election and intimidate the Republic of Tanzania's executive through protests.

Chadema's deputy chairperson John Heche confirmed Pambalu's treason charges, stating he was informed of the situation at a public meeting in Arusha. Heche also anticipates similar charges against himself but vowed not to flee the country, asserting Chadema's commitment to continue their fight.

Pambalu is the second Chadema official to face treason charges, following party leader Tundu Lissu, whose trial is nearing its conclusion. The Chadema party was excluded from the October 2025 vote, which President Samia Suluhu Hassan officially won with 98 percent of the vote.

ma.headline: Morocco raises defense procurement ceiling to MAD 190.5 billion
ma.dek: The 2027 Finance Bill proposes a 21.2% increase for future military equipment and defense industry commitments.
paragraphs: Morocco's draft 2027 Finance Bill proposes raising the ceiling for future military equipment and defense industry commitments by 21.2% to MAD 190.5 billion. This increase of MAD 33.33 billion compares to MAD 157.17 billion in 2026, seeking parliamentary authorization for spending commitments extending into the following financial year. The proposed ceiling has risen from MAD 124.77 billion in 2024 and MAD 133.45 billion in 2025, bringing the cumulative increase over three years to nearly 53%.

Under Article 36, the minister responsible for National Defense would be authorized to enter into commitments during 2027 against appropriations to be allocated in 2028. This authority is for the dedicated account for acquiring and repairing Royal Armed Forces equipment and supporting Morocco’s defense industry. The defense equipment account is separately allocated MAD 11.49 billion in expenditure for 2027.

The Integrated Territorial Development Fund would receive an advance commitment ceiling of MAD 15 billion, the second-largest amount among the provisions. Other authorizations include MAD 3 billion for the Special Roads Fund and MAD 2 billion for prison administration support. The draft also doubles annual expenditure through the Integrated Territorial Development Fund to MAD 10 billion, compared with MAD 5 billion in 2026.

paragraphs: Moroccan Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita spoke by phone on Friday with Russian counterpart Sergei Lavrov about bilateral cooperation and coordination at the United Nations. The call, initiated by Morocco, also covered preparations for the upcoming Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow.

The discussions occurred as UN Security Council members review a US-drafted resolution concerning the Moroccan Sahara. Russia, a permanent Security Council member, will vote on the resolution before MINURSO's mandate expires on October 31.

ma.headline: Morocco's health ministry changed names multiple times
ma.dek: Since independence, the department responsible for health has evolved its name and missions.
paragraphs: Morocco's ministry responsible for health has undergone several name changes since the country gained independence. These shifts reflect the evolving health needs of the population and the changing scope of the ministry's responsibilities. Najib Diouri, an international health economics expert, has examined this evolution.

Diouri's analysis notes that the ministry's leadership has also seen frequent changes, with ministers serving terms ranging from seven days to eight years. This frequent turnover in leadership has accompanied the department's name alterations over time.

The ministry's name changes and evolving missions have occurred as it has adapted to the country's sanitary requirements. The department has consistently worked to meet the health demands of the Moroccan people throughout its history.

ug.headline: Uganda needs Shs118 trillion for climate action
ug.dek: Bank of Uganda partners with European Investment Bank to manage climate risks and attract investment.
paragraphs: Uganda requires approximately Shs118.22 trillion for climate action by 2030, according to figures released on Wednesday. The Bank of Uganda (BoU) and the European Investment Bank (EIB) signed a cooperation agreement in Kampala to strengthen the financial sector's capacity to handle climate-related risks and draw in investment.

The deal will provide technical assistance to the central bank to create a roadmap for greening the financial sector, improve climate-risk disclosure, and enhance reporting by financial institutions. BoU Deputy Governor Prof. Augustus Nuwagaba stated the country must build resilience to climate risks without limiting access to finance.

The partnership will also support the practical use of Uganda’s National Green Taxonomy, launched in September 2025, which defines sustainable economic activities. EIB Vice-President Marko Primorac said the agreement aims to turn climate ambitions into practical tools and boost market confidence.

ug.headline: Museveni asks EU investors to boost Uganda manufacturing
ug.dek: President Museveni urged European investors to expand in manufacturing, energy, and infrastructure to create jobs and grow markets.
paragraphs: President Yoweri Museveni has called on European investors to increase their presence in Uganda's manufacturing, energy, agriculture, and infrastructure sectors. He met with European Union ambassadors and investors at State House Entebbe, emphasizing that productive investment is key to job creation and economic growth. Museveni highlighted Africa's large and growing population as a significant opportunity for European businesses seeking new markets.

The President stressed Uganda's need for investments that boost domestic production and strengthen trade ties with Europe. He welcomed infrastructure projects that connect Uganda to wider markets, stating they benefit both investors and the nation. Museveni also identified the cost of electricity as a barrier for Ugandan manufacturers and called for attention to electricity tariffs, railway transport, and access to financing.

Museveni urged the European Investment Bank to increase funding for strategic infrastructure, including railways and electricity. He also pointed to the Uganda Development Bank as a resource for businesses focused on expanding production and creating jobs. The government reaffirmed its commitment to tax incentives aimed at attracting investment, particularly in manufacturing.

ug.headline: Uganda MPs query Shs41.6 billion diverted by justice ministry
ug.dek: Parliament's Public Accounts Committee found Shs41.6 billion spent without authorisation, contravening the Public Finance Management Act.
paragraphs: Uganda's Parliament has questioned the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs and the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP) for diverting Shs41.6 billion. The funds were reportedly used for activities outside approved work plans without authorisation from the Finance Minister, Henry Musasizi. The Public Accounts Committee, chaired by Hon. Patrick Nsamba, stated this expenditure violated the Public Finance Management Act.

Committee findings, presented on Wednesday, 21 October 2026, revealed the ODPP spent Shs900 million on constructing offices in Katakwi and Yumbe, while the Ministry of Justice diverted Shs40.7 billion. Nsamba noted that savings do not grant authority for unapproved spending, with much of the money allocated to court awards and compensation. The ODPP also faces scrutiny for paying Shs2.95 billion to Graphics Systems for system maintenance without key deliverables being met.

The report highlighted that the ODPP has filled only 600 of its 1,704 approved positions, leading to heavy workloads for prosecutors. The committee recommended enforcing contract liability provisions, recovering funds, and auditing the Prosecution Case Management Information System (PROCAMIS), which has seen Shs42 billion spent since 2017 with reported malfunctions. The Ministry of Justice reported contingent liabilities of Shs3.492 trillion, largely from lawsuits.

ug.headline: Dettol Hygiene Quest expands to 750 Ugandan schools
ug.dek: Over 650,000 pupils will receive hygiene education and handwashing skills in the programme's third phase.
paragraphs: The Dettol Hygiene Quest initiative will reach an additional 650,000 pupils in 750 Ugandan schools through its third phase, launched in 2026. The programme, a partnership between Dettol, the ministry of Education and Sports, and CHIL Hygiene Centre, aims to teach proper hygiene practices to prevent infections.

Organisers stated that the initiative has already reached over one million children in 1,500 schools across Uganda, including in Gulu, Kampala, and Isingiro. Reckitt's country manager for Uganda, Bornface Shaka Onyari, said the new phase will help schools sustain the hygiene practices introduced.

The programme uses an AI-powered chatbot called Keti to support teachers and assess learning outcomes. Aisha Sekindi, representing the state minister for Water, commended the effort but stressed that success should be measured by behavioural change and facility sustainability, not just the number of schools reached.

ug.headline: Museveni commissions $53 million Russian military repair facility
ug.dek: The new facility in Jinja aims to boost Uganda's capacity to maintain military equipment locally.
paragraphs: President Yoweri Museveni commissioned a $53 million military repair facility at Magamaga Cantonment in Jinja District on October 21, 2026. The facility, along with training infrastructure and marine security equipment, was provided through Uganda's defence cooperation with Russia. This development is intended to enhance the Uganda People’s Defence Forces' (UPDF) ability to service military vehicles and equipment within the country.

During the commissioning, President Museveni thanked Russian President Vladimir Putin and a Russian delegation led by Lt Gen Aleksandr Kshimovskii for the military assistance. He expressed a desire for Uganda to develop domestic manufacturing capacity, asking, “What if we made them here with the Russians?” The President stressed the importance of learning from defence partners to reduce reliance on imported equipment and foreign technical expertise.

The two-day engagement, which concluded on October 22, 2026, also included the launch of a digital multimedia training classroom for the BRDM-2MS armoured reconnaissance vehicle at the Mechanised Warfare College in Kalama. In Entebbe, marine operational assets and supporting infrastructure were commissioned, including surveillance radar and eight boats, to strengthen the UPDF’s marine operational capacity.

zw.headline: Comesa businesses seek finance reforms and trade barrier removal
zw.dek: The Comesa Business Council adopted a declaration calling for better access to funding for SMEs, women, and youth.
paragraphs: Regional businesses are pushing for improved access to finance, the removal of trade barriers, and increased investment in industries to boost trade and economic integration across the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa). These proposals are detailed in the Comesa Business Declaration 2026, adopted on October 20 in Harare.

The declaration, released by the Comesa Business Council, specifically calls for coordinated industrial policies and investment in processing facilities. It also demands better access to funding for small and medium enterprises (SMEs), women, youth, and informal businesses to strengthen regional value chains and diversify exports.

Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa assumed the chairmanship of the Comesa Authority for the 2026-2027 period during the 25th Comesa Summit. He pledged to advance the value addition agenda for the region.

cv.headline: Cabo Verde to restart arms control commission
cv.dek: A national commission for light and small arms control will be reactivated to improve coordination and training.
paragraphs: Cabo Verde will restart its national commission for the control of light and small arms and ammunition, a body that had ceased functioning. The recommendation came after a national assessment by the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) which found the lack of such a structure a gap in national coordination. The commission will ensure articulation between institutions responsible for arms management.

Abayomi Adiomi, head of the ECOWAS assessment team, stated that Cabo Verde needs this national commission to coordinate entities involved in arms control. He also highlighted the need to train customs, police, and other relevant professionals, and to provide them with necessary equipment. Camilo da Graça from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Defence confirmed the reactivation, adding that the National Police will lead the interministerial and interdisciplinary body.

The commission will monitor arms and ammunition management and produce reports for comparison with other ECOWAS member states. The United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR) representative, Mohamed Coulibaly, stressed the importance of improved information sharing and operational coordination. Measures identified include awareness campaigns, voluntary arms collection, and destruction of obsolete or seized weapons, building on the 2023 law on arms and ammunition.

cv.headline: Cape Verde hosts national gymnastics championship
cv.dek: 18 athletes from Santiago Sul, Santiago Norte, and São Vicente compete for national titles.
paragraphs: Praia will host the 26th National Gymnastics Championship on Saturday, October 24, at the Vavá Duarte Sports Pavilion. 18 gymnasts aged 12 and older, representing regional associations from Santiago Sul, Santiago Norte, and São Vicente, will compete. The event is organized by the Cape Verdean Gymnastics Federation (FCG).

The competition follows the All-Around classification format, using the International Gymnastics Federation's scoring code for 2025-2028. A jury will evaluate the athletes, who qualified through their respective regional championships. The championship aims to assess technical progress and identify potential national team members for international competitions.

Wânia Monteiro, president of the FCG, stated that the championship is a moment to showcase the year's work from clubs across different islands. She emphasized its importance in celebrating national gymnastics and encouraging more young people to participate in the sport. Awards will be presented on Saturday evening.

The driver involved in the accident, a young man, was detained by the National Police and is awaiting the outcome of the process in preventive detention. The incident occurred as the child was crossing a pedestrian crossing and was struck by a vehicle traveling at high speed.

td.headline: Chad parliament launches breast and cervical cancer screening
td.dek: Lawmakers commit to improving healthcare access and funding for women's health programs.
paragraphs: Chad's National Assembly hosted a "Pink October" awareness day on October 23, 2026, focusing on fighting breast and cervical cancers. Dr. Mahamat Abakar Kori, the 4th vice-president, spoke at the event, which included voluntary screening sessions. The assembly pledged to strengthen healthcare services, improve financial access to treatment, and support prevention programs nationwide.

Dr. Kori highlighted that many Chadian women suffer in silence, often seeking medical help at advanced stages of cancer due to societal taboos, lack of information, and limited access to early detection, especially in rural areas. He emphasized that screening is an act of courage and responsibility, saving lives and preventing family tragedies.

The National Assembly committed to equipping health facilities with modern diagnostic tools, exploring universal health coverage mechanisms, enhancing medical staff training, and ensuring sustained funding for health initiatives. This multisectoral effort calls for the involvement of traditional and religious leaders to combat stigma surrounding women's cancers.

td.headline: APET launches activities to boost Chad's education system
td.dek: The non-profit association aims to improve access to quality education for all Chadian children and youth.
paragraphs: The Association Agir pour l'Éducation au Tchad (APET) officially launched its activities in N'Djamena on Friday, October 23, 2026. The non-profit, apolitical, and non-confessional organization aims to transform interest in education into concrete contributions for the country's development.

APET's president, Allayanmal Kladegue, outlined the association's vision to ensure every Chadian child and young person has access to quality education, covering formal schooling, vocational training, literacy, and intergenerational learning. The organization's work will focus on six priority areas, including promoting access for vulnerable groups and girls, supporting local initiatives, and strengthening the capacities of educators.

The association plans to build a network of skills, forge institutional partnerships, and implement pilot actions like tutoring and mentoring. APET also announced the upcoming creation of a Citizenship and Education Laboratory and has a platform for public membership to support its mission.

dj.headline: Djibouti fund backs 15 community projects
dj.dek: The Community Development Fund has now supported 52 local initiatives since its launch.
paragraphs: Djibouti's Agency for Social Development (ADDS) has signed agreements with 15 associations to fund local development projects. The Community Development Fund (FDC) allocated 20 million Djiboutian francs (FDJ) for these 15 sub-projects, each proposed by an association from the program's intervention zones. The initiative aims to support local efforts and increase resident involvement in neighborhood development.

The signing ceremony was attended by parliamentarians, the mayor of Balbala commune, local officials, and directors from ADDS and the French Development Agency (AFD). Representatives from the beneficiary associations were also present. Speakers praised the quality of the selected projects and urged the recipients to manage the funds responsibly and execute their plans effectively.

This marks the third call for projects by the FDC, bringing the total number of funded initiatives to 52 since its inception. The cumulative amount disbursed for these projects now stands at 57.97 million FDJ.

Ntshangase's goal marks his return to professional football after a three-year break, having joined Amawele from SAFA Limpopo ABC Motsepe League side Mohlabile United.
Amawele's win follows a 1-0 victory over Pigg’s Peak Professionals last week. The league's top goalscorer this season is guaranteed a revised E15 000 prize.

sz.headline: Eswatini football team faces E1 million travel bill for Malta match
sz.dek: Sihlangu Semnikati will make history on November 12, 2026, playing their first international friendly against a European nation.
paragraphs: Eswatini's senior men's national football team, Sihlangu Semnikati, faces an estimated travel bill exceeding E1 million for their upcoming friendly match against Malta. The team is scheduled to play the European side on Thursday, November 12, 2026, at the Ta’ Qali National Stadium. Round-trip flights for a delegation of 30 individuals are projected to cost over E1 million.

Eswatini Football Association (EFA) Marketing and Communications Officer Muzi ‘Rhoo’ Radebe confirmed a signed agreement between the associations but declined to share specific details, stating that logistics will be guided by the contract. Typically, the visiting national association covers its own international airfare and transit costs, while the host nation provides accommodation, meals, and ground transport.

This fixture marks the first time Eswatini will play an international friendly match against a European nation. The match is crucial preparation for Malta, currently ranked 160th in FIFA, ahead of their UEFA Nations League clash against Gibraltar on November 16. Malta leads their group with seven points from three matches and is on a four-match unbeaten streak.

sz.headline: Eswatini minister highlights vast CEO to worker pay gaps
sz.dek: Minister Manqoba Khumalo stated some CEOs earn E280,000 while lowest paid workers take home E3,500.
paragraphs: Minister for Commerce, Industry and Trade Manqoba Khumalo explained that Eswatini's economic growth does not benefit ordinary workers due to vast salary disparities in some companies. He noted the absence of formal salary structures means the gap between chief executive officers and the lowest-paid employees is determined solely by management. Khumalo cited an example where a CEO earns E280,000 while a worker receives E3,500, meaning the boss earns 80 times more.

Speaking at a breakfast meeting in Ezulwini, Khumalo stated that in companies with such gaps, economic growth benefits only high earners, leaving those at the bottom unaffected. The World Bank projects Eswatini's economy to grow by five percent, its strongest since 2019, yet over half of emaSwati live below the poverty line. Khumalo previously stated in August that income inequality remains a significant challenge, with growth benefits not always distributed equally.

Khumalo pointed out that pay gaps have been closed in developed countries. He previously served as Coca-Cola's general manager in Ireland before becoming a senator and minister in Eswatini. Economists are observing Eswatini's growth but questioning its distribution. The minister stressed that continued attention is needed to achieve more inclusive economic growth.

sz.headline: dagga trade fuels sex work in Madlangampisi

Alex Tsabedze, the Indvuna Yenkhundla for Madlangampisi, confirmed the presence of sex workers, noting a change in the town's social environment and increased visibility of young women after dark. Residents also expressed worry about young girls allegedly forming relationships with dagga farmers and older men attracted by the trade's profits.

Police have been targeting illegal dagga cultivation and trafficking around Madlangampisi, destroying hectares of plants and arresting individuals for smuggling. Some seized drug consignments have been valued at millions of Emalangeni, reinforcing the perception of a significant illegal industry.

ga.headline: Gabon launches digital platform for public services
ga.dek: Gabon Connect aims to simplify administrative tasks, secure public revenue, and improve the business environment.
paragraphs: Gabon launched its digital platform, Gabon Connect, on Thursday, October 22, 2026, in Libreville. The platform integrates services like Déclaration unique des salaires (DUS) and TrésorPay to streamline administrative processes and enhance public revenue collection. Vice-president Hermann Immongault presented the initiative, which aims to simplify procedures, reduce processing times, and improve the overall business climate.

The Gabon Connect platform will progressively consolidate digitized public services onto a single online interface. It includes six key services: eTax for taxes, eEmployeur for social formalities, TrésorPay for non-fiscal revenues, eDouane for customs, and ePropriété for land registry. The full deployment is scheduled to conclude by December 2027, with the goal of reducing physical travel and procedural complexity for citizens and businesses.

Beyond administrative simplification, Gabon Connect is designed to improve oversight of fiscal, customs, and non-fiscal revenues. The introduction of DUS and TrésorPay specifically targets the security of collections and transparency in public fund management. This digital transformation is seen as a strategic lever to de-silo services, ensure reliable information, and boost public action efficiency, according to Immongault.
ga.body:
Gabon launched its digital platform, Gabon Connect, on Thursday, October 22, 2026, in Libreville. The platform integrates services like Déclaration unique des salaires (DUS) and TrésorPay to streamline administrative processes and enhance public revenue collection. Vice-president Hermann Immongault presented the initiative, which aims to simplify procedures, reduce processing times, and improve the overall business climate.

The Gabon Connect platform will progressively consolidate digitized public services onto a single online interface. It includes six key services: eTax for taxes, eEmployeur for social formalities, TrésorPay for non-fiscal revenues, eDouane for customs, and ePropriété for land registry. The full deployment is scheduled to conclude by December 2027, with the goal of reducing physical travel and procedural complexity for citizens and businesses.

Beyond administrative simplification, Gabon Connect is designed to improve oversight of fiscal, customs, and non-fiscal revenues. The introduction of DUS and TrésorPay specifically targets the security of collections and transparency in public fund management. This digital transformation is seen as a strategic lever to de-silo services, ensure reliable information, and boost public action efficiency, according to Immongault.

ga.headline: Gabon youth fight female cancers in Mouila
ga.dek: Over 300 young people learned about prevention and risks during a three-day awareness marathon.
paragraphs: In Mouila, Gabon, the Jeunes Capables collective organized a three-day awareness marathon in secondary schools to combat female cancers. The initiative, which concluded on October 17, aimed to educate over 300 young people about prevention and associated risks. Dr. Aubin Djembi informed students about the causes, risk factors, and consequences of breast and cervical cancers, stressing the importance of early detection and regular medical follow-ups.

Philippe Arnaud Nziengui, president of Jeunes Capables, expressed satisfaction with the high participation of the target audience. The event highlighted the ongoing challenge of promoting early detection for improved recovery chances in Gabon, where diagnostic delays and limited access to specialized exams persist. Cultural barriers and fear of results can also deter women from seeking medical care.

Globocan estimates that Gabon records approximately 295 new cases of breast cancer and 146 new cases of cervical cancer annually. The initiative by Jeunes Capables shows that the fight against female cancers requires information and community mobilization, alongside effective access to healthcare. Medical specialists emphasize that screening should extend beyond October, with any unusual symptoms warranting a consultation.

ga.headline: Gabon warns against illegal land sales at Cap Santa Clara
ga.dek: The Ministry of Housing alerts residents to irregular occupations that threaten government development projects.
paragraphs: Gabon's Ministry of Housing, Habitat, Urbanism, and Land Registry issued a warning on October 23 regarding illegal land sales and occupations at Cap Santa Clara. The ministry stated that these irregular practices threaten government urbanization and development projects in the area. The alert aims to preserve the integrity of public land operations and remind citizens of the rules governing land transactions and construction.

The ministry detailed that land sales or transfers must be conducted by legally authorized individuals with proper land titles or administrative acts. Occupying a plot of land also requires legal standing, and any construction must adhere to existing regulations, including obtaining building permits. The warning emphasizes that fraudulent sales, illegal occupations, and unauthorized constructions can lead to land evacuation and building demolition without compensation.

This official statement serves as a deterrent against dubious transactions and aims to protect buyers from losing their investments. The government is urging the public to remain vigilant and refrain from any anarchic initiatives that could result in demolitions and evictions. The ministry's action is intended to safeguard planned public developments at Cap Santa Clara and prevent land disputes.

gm.headline: Coalition 2026 unveils 66 actions for Gambia by 2031
gm.dek: The manifesto, titled ‘The Gambia We Deserve’, outlines three pillars and 13 policy points.
paragraphs: Coalition 2026, led by UNITE leader Talib Ahmed Bensouda, launched its manifesto ‘The Gambia We Deserve’ on October 22, 2026. The plan details 3 pillars, 13 policy points, and 66 priority actions to be completed by 2031. Bensouda stated the manifesto is built around governance and trust, human development, and economic integrity.

The manifesto includes a constitutional review within two years and aims to raise health spending to 15% of the budget. A National Development Bank will be established to boost job creation and economic growth. Bensouda explained the 66 actions align with The Gambia’s age of 66 in 2031, when the plan concludes.

Bensouda highlighted current challenges including a high cost of living, youth unemployment, and difficulties in farming. He noted that despite the country's potential and hard-working population, families struggle and young people seek opportunities. The coalition aims to transform The Gambia by turning potential into progress and resources into opportunity.

gm.headline: Gambia highlights slave trade heritage sites
gm.dek: The National Centre for Arts and Culture promotes Kunta Kinteh Island and Wassu Stone Circles for tourism.
paragraphs: The Director General of The Gambia's National Centre for Arts and Culture, Hassoum Ceesay, is promoting two UNESCO World Heritage Sites to boost tourism beyond beaches. Ceesay highlighted Kunta Kinteh Island, formerly James Island, which served as a departure point during the Transatlantic Slave Trade. He also discussed the Wassu Stone Circles, an archaeological site.

Ceesay described Kunta Kinteh Island as a place of "horror and terror," where captives were held in dungeons before being transported to the New World. The island, renamed in 2011 to honor Alex Haley's "Roots" hero, is compared to Goree Island in Senegal and Elmina Castle in Ghana. The government plans to enhance the island's appeal and educational value.

The Wassu Stone Circles are also a UNESCO World Heritage Site, though Ceesay provided fewer details on this location in the interview. The NCAC aims to showcase these cultural assets to Gambians and the world, moving tourism beyond traditional sun and beach offerings.

gm.headline: Gambia civic leaders urge tolerance before 2026 election
gm.dek: National Council for Civic Education warns 35 constituencies are high-risk for electoral violence.
paragraphs: Gambian civic leaders are calling for tolerance and unity ahead of the December 5, 2026 presidential election. At a workshop, Chief Civic Education Officer Yusupha Bojang warned against divisive language in political discourse, stating elections should be a marketplace of ideas, not a battleground for insults or polarization.

Bojang revealed that early warning analysis shows 35 of the country’s 53 constituencies are rated high or very high risk, a concern requiring vigilance from all stakeholders. He urged political leaders to publicly condemn hate speech, reminding them that rivals are not enemies.

The Inter-Party Committee (IPC) also reaffirmed its dedication to fostering peace, inclusivity, and mutual respect. Pamela Camara of Catholic Relief Services stressed that peace is nurtured daily, urging citizens to use their voices for healing and trust.

gm.headline: Gambia finance minister proposes D66.78B budget
gm.dek: The proposed 2027 national budget includes D16.17 billion for debt servicing and D6.06 billion for education.
paragraphs: The Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs will present the 2027 national budget of D66.78 billion to the National Assembly today. This represents a 12.5 per cent increase from the D59.36 billion approved for 2026.

Initial estimates show debt servicing will be the largest expenditure at D16.17 billion, about one-third of the D48.6 billion financed directly by the government. Basic and secondary education receives the largest sectoral allocation with D6.06 billion, followed by health at D4.10 billion.

The budget projects domestic revenue at D37.39 billion, with tax revenue expected to rise to D31.47 billion. Total revenue and grants are projected at D56.94 billion, leading to a gross budget deficit of D2.30 billion, or 0.99 per cent of the projected GDP. The government plans to borrow D7.63 billion domestically and D2.21 billion from foreign sources.

gm.headline: Gambia electoral commission delays voter roll release
gm.dek: The Independent Electoral Commission cannot release raw voter data until court revisions are complete for the December 2026 election.
paragraphs: The Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) in Gambia will not release raw voter roll data until Revising Courts finish their hearings and magistrates sign off on necessary changes. This decision comes amid calls for transparency ahead of the December 2026 presidential election. The IEC chairman stated on Thursday that the commission must first receive directions on which names to keep or remove from the register before finalizing the voter count.

IEC chairman explained that releasing the data prematurely would be illogical, as the final number of registered voters can only be determined after legal revisions. He assured stakeholders that the data will be shared with all political parties once the process is concluded, noting that magistrates are still actively handling cases before the Revising Courts. The commission has established procedures for providing voter information to parties and other election participants.

The IEC is also addressing other electoral preparations, including polling station arrangements and the involvement of political parties and their agents. The chairman emphasized the commission's commitment to making the election as inclusive as possible and urged stakeholders to consider the practical challenges of election preparation. The completion of the Revising Courts' work remains a prerequisite for releasing the raw voter roll data.

gn.headline: Dubreka arts institute official dies in road accident
gn.dek: Amadou Bah, deputy director general for studies at ISAMK, died Friday after his tricycle collided with a military convoy.
paragraphs: Amadou Bah, the deputy director general for studies at the Mory Kanté Higher Institute of Arts (ISAMK) in Dubreka, died on Friday, October 23, 2026. The accident occurred in Kénendé, on the road between Dubreka and Kagbelen, when the tricycle he was travelling in collided with a military convoy.

Bah was on his way to Conakry for a funeral when the crash happened. He sustained severe injuries, including fractures and internal bleeding, and was taken to the Dubreka prefectural hospital. Medical staff attempted to save him, but he succumbed to his injuries.

His colleagues expressed shock, having seen him participating in institute activities just hours before. Bah was considered a key figure in the ISAMK administration, and his death is a significant loss for the university community in Dubreka and Guinea's higher education sector.

gw.dek: 18 health professionals provided consultations and health education on scalp ringworm at SOS School.
paragraphs: The 21st Chinese Medical Team held a child health seminar at SOS School in Bissau on Friday, October 23, 2026, offering free medical consultations and promoting Traditional Chinese Medicine. The initiative involved 18 health professionals from the Military Hospital and Canchungo Regional Hospital, who also distributed footballs and school supplies to children.

The seminar focused on preventing scalp ringworm, a common childhood illness during the rainy season, detailing its symptoms, transmission, and the importance of early diagnosis and treatment. Doctor Wang Weicheng advised students to avoid contact with infected animals, refrain from sharing personal items, and maintain a clean, dry scalp, noting the disease's prevalence in the Bijagós Archipelago.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau police rescue 71 trafficking victims
gw.dek: Operation ASTRA dismantled a human trafficking ring that lured victims with promises of work abroad.
paragraphs: Police in Guinea-Bissau rescued 71 people from various West African nations on October 22, 2026, in an operation that dismantled a human trafficking network. The operation, named ASTRA, led to the arrest of four suspects. The victims, originally from Mali, Guinea, Burkina Faso, Togo, Senegal, and Sierra Leone, were lured with promises of jobs in Canada, Europe, and the United States.

According to the Judicial Police (PJ) spokesperson Braima Cissé, the victims were brought to Bissau and held against their will. PJ agent António Gomes told AFP that the victims faced physical and psychological pressure, including threats and abuse, and were forced into pyramid schemes to recruit new members via social media. The network allegedly provided false office details in Canada, the United States, and Portugal to appear legitimate.

Interpol's information aided the dismantling of the network, which investigators believe operated across several countries in the sub-region. The rescued individuals will be handed over to their respective embassies, with others needing to contact family for assistance to return home.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau groups demand political prisoner release
gw.dek: Organisations sent a manifesto to ECOWAS mediators calling for democratic freedoms and an end to detentions.
paragraphs: Political and civic groups in Guinea-Bissau demanded the immediate release of all political prisoners on October 23, 2026. The groups, part of the Frente Única and the Rede Internacional de Solidariedade com a Guiné-Bissau, asked the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) to intervene. They stated that continued detention contradicts court decisions.

The manifesto, delivered to ECOWAS mediators in Dakar and Senegalese embassies in five cities including Bissau, also called for the full restoration of fundamental freedoms and political activities. It specifically requested the reopening of political party headquarters and the lifting of restrictions on civil society and media organisations. The groups expressed dissatisfaction with the perceived lack of impartiality from the Senegalese mediation, accusing it of being too close to the current government.

Signatories include API-Cabas Garandi, PAIGC, and UNTG-CS, along with international solidarity groups. They urged ECOWAS to engage with the military command to restore constitutional order, respecting the popular vote from November 2025. The document also proposed individual sanctions against those obstructing the restoration of constitutional normality.

gw.headline: PRS youth wings agree to unified congress
gw.dek: Factions associated with Franco Ialá and Ednilson Alberto Nambeia have committed to ending internal divisions within the party.
paragraphs: The youth wing of Guinea-Bissau's Social Renovation Party (PRS), known as JRS, announced on October 23, 2026, that internal divisions have ended, forming a single youth organization. Representatives from factions linked to Franco Ialá and Ednilson Alberto Nambeia formalized this decision in Bissau, agreeing to work together for the party's reunification.

In a document, the youth declared their split "free, definitive and irreversible" and will act as facilitators for party reunification. They will form a Joint Youth Commission to draft a roadmap for a unified and inclusive congress, committing to cease mutual attacks on social media and public spaces, and to avoid participating in separate congresses.

The JRS is calling on the two wings of the party's Superior Directorate to negotiate a unified congress. The youth have pledged to uphold unity, dialogue, forgiveness, and the collective interest over personal or group ambitions for the full reunification of the PRS.

lr.headline: Liberia summons health officials over Ebola preparedness
lr.dek: Lawmakers want details on response measures amid Nigeria outbreak and Bundibugyo Ebola concerns.
paragraphs: Liberia's House of Representatives has summoned health authorities to a briefing on the nation's readiness for public health emergencies. The decision followed reports of a confirmed Ebola case in Nigeria and an ongoing outbreak in Bundibugyo. The Minister of Health and the Director General of the National Public Health Institute of Liberia (NPHIL) are expected to appear before the House on Tuesday, October 27.

Montserrado County Representative Dixon Seboe requested the briefing, citing the need for detailed information on preparedness, including medical supplies, trained personnel, and emergency response resources. He also wants updates on disease surveillance, laboratory testing capacity, and the availability of isolation facilities across Liberia's 15 counties. Border and port health authorities will also explain screening procedures.

The summons also seeks information on public awareness campaigns, infection prevention supplies, frontline health worker training, and resources for enforcing preventive directives. Seboe also called for details on measures to protect public schools, markets, and densely populated areas, particularly in Montserrado County.

lr.headline: Liberian economist Jackson seeks travel for medical treatment
lr.dek: Samuel Jackson, facing charges in his wife's death, asked a court for permission to leave Liberia for medical care.
paragraphs: Liberian economist Samuel Jackson appealed to Criminal Court “A” for permission to travel abroad for medical treatment on October 22, 2026. Jackson, who is facing charges in connection with his wife Ntombi Khumalo Jackson’s March 2026 death, cited deteriorating health. He was seen struggling to walk at the Temple of Justice in Monrovia.

Jackson is seeking specialized medical care outside Liberia but remains barred from leaving the country due to ongoing legal proceedings. His wife, a South African attorney, was found dead in their Monrovia home with reports of severe head injuries. Jackson maintains her injuries resulted from an accidental fall.

The economist was released in April on a US$20,000 bond with travel restrictions and mandatory court check-ins. He has accused the prosecution of being politically motivated to silence his criticism of President Joseph Boakai’s administration. Authorities have not yet released the official autopsy findings.

lr.headline: hundreds stranded on zwედru highway
lr.dek: hundreds of vehicles and travelers have been stuck for over a week on the Ganta–Zwedru Highway.
paragraphs: Hundreds of travelers and motorists are stranded for days on the road linking Monrovia to Zwedru, Grand Gedeh, as deteriorating conditions have cut off the highway in several sections. Commercial vehicles, private cars, and passengers are affected by the muddy and swampy terrain, particularly between Toe Town and Zwedru. Some travelers have been waiting for over a week for the road to become passable.

More than 150 vehicles were reportedly trapped in muddy conditions between Duogee Town and Senneh-wen in Grand Gedeh County, according to reports. Travelers are calling on the Ministry of Public Works to intervene urgently, warning that prolonged delays are contributing to food shortages and rising prices. The ministry stated on October 21 that a team was working to stabilize a 100-meter swampy section near Duogee Town.

The highway serves as a critical transportation corridor for southeastern Liberia, affecting the movement of agricultural produce, food supplies, and fuel. The recurring deterioration is linked to heavy rainfall and poor drainage. Travelers are urging the Ministry of Public Works to restore passage quickly to prevent further hardship for passengers, traders, and residents.

lr.headline: Liberia minister nominee promises price transparency
lr.dek: Stephen M. Yekeson Jr. pledges to publish weekly prices for rice, fuel, and cement in all 15 counties within 100 days.
paragraphs: Liberia's acting Commerce and Industry Minister Designate Stephen M. Yekeson Jr. told senators on Wednesday that he will publish weekly prices for rice, fuel, and cement in all 15 counties within 100 days. Yekeson also pledged to protect consumers and enforce Liberian-only business sectors. He aims for Liberia to produce more of what it consumes by 2029.

Yekeson admitted that prices have continued to rise despite a stronger Liberian Dollar, which closed September at L$172 to US$1. Small traders report wholesalers still price stock at L$190 to the dollar, a gap of nearly 12 percent. A Senate probe found diesel prices rose 47 percent between October 2024 and September 2026.

The minister nominee plans to review pricing with the Liberia Petroleum Refining Company (LPRC) and ensure regulated prices reflect import costs, duties, transport, and a reasonable margin. World rice prices have increased by about 67 percent on the year, hitting a 26-month high in early October.

lr.headline: Liberia anti-corruption chief sees US$5 billion revenue potential
lr.dek: Arthur Fumbah of the LACC stated that a corruption-free Liberia could boost annual revenue to US$5 billion.
paragraphs: Achieving a corruption-free Liberia is possible with stronger coordination among oversight institutions, the Legislature, and the Judiciary, according to Arthur W.B. Fumbah, Executive Vice Chairperson of the Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission (LACC). Fumbah spoke at a policy dialogue in Monrovia on October 23, 2026, emphasizing that institutional cooperation and preventive measures are key to combating corruption.

Fumbah argued that eliminating corruption could significantly increase Liberia’s annual revenue to as much as US$5 billion, a substantial rise from recent efforts to reach US$1 billion. He criticized weak penalties for corruption, citing a Supreme Court ruling where a convicted official was ordered to pay US$10,000, which he said undermines accountability given the costs of investigations.

He also called for a review of the Public Financial Management Law, suggesting that heads of institutions influencing the appointment of accountants and auditors creates corruption opportunities. Fumbah proposed that the Comptroller General’s Office and other agencies deploy qualified professionals to public institutions to strengthen oversight and reduce financial misconduct.

Business leaders from Libya and Indonesia attended the signing ceremony, which was preceded by bilateral B2B meetings. ly.headline: UNSMIL warns against forceful CBL leadership change
ly.dek: The UN mission stresses operational independence and integrity of the Central Bank of Libya are essential for economic stability.
paragraphs: The United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) stated today that it notes developments regarding the House of Representatives Presidency's decision on the Central Bank of Libya (CBL) leadership. This follows the forceful installation yesterday of Fawzi Abu Khazam as a new interim CBL Governor.

UNSMIL emphasized that the CBL's operational independence and integrity are essential to protect public resources, maintain economic stability, and ensure credibility with international financial partners. Any leadership changes must be driven by a commitment to improved governance and oversight to maintain confidence in the management of monetary policy and reserves.

The mission warned that continued pressure on the CBL to finance escalating public expenditure is unsustainable and could intensify exchange rate pressures, fuel inflation, and deplete reserves, potentially inflicting increased economic hardship and social unrest. UNSMIL urged all stakeholders to follow Libyan legal procedures to protect the CBL's credibility.

mg.headline: Madagascar arrests prison officials over Chinese escape
mg.dek: Three prison administrators face charges after 11 Chinese nationals disappeared from Avaradrano prison.
paragraphs: Madagascar has arrested three prison administration officials and placed 12 others under judicial supervision following the irregular release and subsequent disappearance of 11 Chinese nationals. The arrests followed their presentation to the Anosy prosecutor's office on Friday. The 11 Chinese men had left Avaradrano prison in August, reportedly as transfers, without proper authorization. Two extradition waves to China occurred in September, with two of these inmates expected to be among those sent back.

The disappearance of the inmates was only publicly revealed in October, prompting swift administrative and legal action. Among those detained are former Avaradrano prison director Mamisoa Tolojanahary, director of prison administration Jean De Kopy Rajaonarison, and the head of the Antanimora post. The first substitute prosecutor, Nirina Andrianarivony, stated that several suspects remain at large, including Mahomed Razafimbeloson, secretary-general of the prison agents' union, who is wanted on an arrest warrant.

Mahomed Razafimbeloson has accused Minister of Justice Fanirisoa Ernaivo of issuing instructions for the inmates' release, a claim the minister has categorically denied. The case has raised questions about the effectiveness of surveillance mechanisms and inter-service communication, especially given the speed of the current prosecutions compared to the months of silence. This controversy impacts the country's image, particularly concerning corruption concerns voiced by the president of the Refondation.

mg.headline: Madagascar customs union decries accusations
mg.dek: The union says generalized criticism of customs officers is unfair and demands more resources.
paragraphs: The Syndicate of Customs Inspectors of Madagascar (SIDM) has responded to widespread criticism of the customs administration, particularly concerning gold trafficking allegations. The union stated that responsibilities should be determined through legal investigations, not public accusations that tarnish the reputation of all customs officers. The SIDM insists that facts must be verified before public statements are made, citing recent gold seizures as examples of how imprecise communication can be harmful.

Recent incidents, including the interception of nearly six kilograms of gold at Ivato on September 13, which led to charges against five customs officers and two airport security agents, have placed airport controls under scrutiny. Another seizure of 2.85 kilograms of gold on October 22 has renewed questions about surveillance effectiveness. The SIDM argues that these cases highlight a need for clearer division of responsibilities among border security agencies.

The SIDM reports that approximately 700 customs agents are currently responsible for border control, an insufficient number for the required level of inspection. A recruitment drive is planned to increase staffing. The union also seeks improved working conditions, clearly defined rules, and better support from management for its members, emphasizing that the fight against illegal practices must be balanced with protecting officers' rights and strengthening operational capacities.

mw.headline: Malawi fuel black market fuels deadly fires
mw.dek: Fuel shortages in Malawi's formal supply chain are driving a dangerous black market trade that has led to a vendor's death.
paragraphs: Malawi's fuel crisis has worsened, with long queues at filling stations and widespread shortages. This scarcity is pushing transport costs higher and disrupting businesses. Meanwhile, fuel is readily available on the black market at two to three times the official pump price, raising questions about diversion and regulatory failures.

A fuel vendor died last Monday in Kanengo, Lilongwe, after his motorcycle, carrying fuel in 20-litre containers, crashed during a police pursuit. His companion suffered serious burns in the incident. This tragedy highlights the public safety emergency created by the illegal fuel trade, beyond economic damage.

Civil society groups like the Human Rights Consultative Committee (HRCC) have spoken out about the crisis. Authorities, including the Malawi Energy Regulatory Authority (Mera) and the Malawi Police Service, are urged to investigate fuel diversion and enforce laws against illegal trading. No profit from this trade is worth a human life.

mw.headline: Malawi chief dies in India after treatment
mw.dek: Inkosi Chindi, 49, passed away on October 23, 2026, while receiving medical care arranged by the Malawi Government.
paragraphs: Inkosi Chindi of Mzimba died in India on Friday, October 23, 2026, where he had traveled for medical treatment facilitated by the Malawi Government. The traditional leader, born May 5, 1977, was 49 years old at the time of his death. His passing was confirmed by Mmbelwa District Council District Commissioner Emmanuel Bulukutu and Ngoni Chiefs Council Secretary Inkosi Jalavikuwa.

Inkosi Jalavikuwa stated that details surrounding the chief's illness and death were not disclosed but confirmed he died while receiving treatment. Burial arrangements will be announced once the process of repatriating the chief's remains to Malawi is complete. His death is considered a significant loss for the traditional leadership in Mzimba.

The Ngoni Chiefs Council and relevant authorities are expected to provide further details on the repatriation process and the funeral programme. The nation awaits official communication regarding arrangements to honour the late traditional leader.

mw.headline: vandals cut water at Malawi's largest hospital
mw.dek: Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital suspended activities as dry taps hit patients and staff during 35°C heat.
paragraphs: Patients and guardians at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital (QECH) in Blantyre scrambled for water on Friday as temperatures reached 35°C. The hospital's taps ran dry due to vandals damaging Blantyre Water Board (BWB) pipelines, forcing a reduction in pumping capacity.

The water shortage led QECH, Malawi's largest referral hospital, to suspend some activities. Director General Professor Patrick Kamalo confirmed the hospital had run out of water, impacting patients, guardians, and health workers struggling with hygiene and the heat. Some patients were reportedly turned away.

One guardian, Lucia Jasi, was instructed by nurses to fetch water from her home borehole, noting that patients from distant districts could not do the same. Another guardian, Maureen Kagona, said she had not bathed due to the shortage. Health sciences students also struggled to concentrate while searching for drinking water.

mw.headline: Malawi withdraws ICC judicial candidate
mw.dek: Tujilane Chizumila was nominated in March but removed from the race before December elections.
paragraphs: Malawi has withdrawn its candidate, Ms Tujilane Chizumila, from the running for a position as a judge at the International Criminal Court. The Embassy of the Republic of Malawi announced the decision on 20 October 2026, removing the country from contention in the court’s ninth election of judges. The ICC’s governing body, the Assembly of States Parties, recorded the withdrawal in official documents on the same day.

Ms Chizumila was nominated by the Government of Malawi in a communication dated 27 March 2026. The notice of withdrawal provided no specific reason for the decision. Judges at the ICC, which is based in The Hague, are elected by member states for nine-year terms.

The election of new judges is scheduled to occur during the twenty-fifth session of the Assembly of States Parties in New York. This session is set to run from 7 to 17 December 2026. The ICC prosecutes genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and the crime of aggression.

ml.dek: The foundation provided food, equipment for women's groups, and medical consultations in Koulikoro.
paragraphs: The Orange Mali Foundation has allocated 25 million FCFA to support vulnerable populations in Koulikoro through donations of food, equipment for women's groups, and free medical consultations. This initiative, launched on Friday, October 23, 2026, aims to assist thousands of beneficiaries over two days.

On the first day, 17 million FCFA was dedicated to supporting social and associative structures, with aid intended to improve living conditions. Koniba Diarra, representing beneficiary associations, expressed gratitude for the foundation's commitment. Mohamed Koureichi, regional director of social development for Koulikoro, highlighted the importance of this contribution in supporting families and individuals facing social difficulties.

The foundation's general administrator, Djénébou Diallo, stated that this mobilization is part of 20 years of engagement with Malian populations. The total 25 million FCFA will fund two major actions in the Koulikoro region, with the first 17 million FCFA directly benefiting over 5,000 people.

ml.headline: Malian media figure Abdoulaye Benson Diakité dies
ml.dek: The former RFI journalist and institutional communication advisor passed away on October 23, 2026, in Bamako.
paragraphs: Abdoulaye Benson Diakité, a prominent Malian journalist and communicator, died on Friday, October 23, 2026, in Bamako. Diakité, a former presenter for Radio France Internationale (RFI), had a career spanning decades in media, institutional communication, and culture. His funeral was scheduled for Friday after prayers in Missabougou.

Born in Bancoumana, Diakité began his career in teaching before moving into media, working at Africa N°1 and Radio Télévision Gabonaise in Gabon. He later joined RFI in France from 1994 to 2009, co-hosting programs like "Plein Sud" and focusing on African societies, culture, and diasporas. After returning to Mali, he served as a technical advisor in the General Secretariat of the Presidency in January 2010 and later as a special advisor to President Amadou Toumani Touré in August 2011.

Diakité also contributed to Malian media, sharing his insights on TM1 in recent years. He remained active in cultural initiatives, notably spearheading the Festi’Bazin in 2014 to promote Malian bazin fabric and its artisans. His career bridged international newsrooms and Malian realities, emphasizing knowledge transmission and giving voice to others.

ml.headline: Mali minister launches sixth 'Consume Local' month
ml.dek: Minister Moussa Alassane Diallo announced 100 million FCFA for local businesses and artisans.
paragraphs: Mali's Minister of Industry and Commerce, Moussa Alassane Diallo, launched the sixth national "Consume Local" month on October 15, 2026. The ceremony, held at the Chamber of Commerce and Industry, aimed to promote Malian products and economic sovereignty. The event also included the presentation of a locally made outfit to the Head of State.

Minister Diallo highlighted the government's commitment to supporting micro, small, and medium enterprises, artisans, and agricultural cooperatives. A budget of 100 million FCFA has been allocated this year to support these local actors. Public procurement will also be directed towards "Made in Mali" products.

mr.headline: Mauritania minister's niece withdraws from Morocco study place amid controversy
mr.dek: Zahra Al-Tayeb Amin renounces a doctoral enrollment in Morocco after a classmate questioned selection criteria.
paragraphs: Zahra Al-Tayeb Amin, niece of the Minister of Higher Education Yacoub Ould Meïne, has withdrawn her enrollment for doctoral studies in Morocco. The decision follows a public dispute with classmate Belkis Abdallahi El Adel, who claimed she was more qualified for the opportunity. The controversy centers on the selection process for a study place in Morocco, with El Adel asserting she was first in their master's promotion and Amin second.

Amin stated that the faculty had not published an official ranking among the three eligible students and that the opportunity was an enrollment place, not a scholarship as initially claimed. She also noted administrative hurdles due to her new training role within the Ministry of Social Action, Childhood, and Family. Amin announced she would pursue a scholarship offer from Utah State University in the United States instead.

El Adel rejected Amin's explanations, insisting her objection was about selection criteria, not a personal dispute. She pointed to an official university list ranking candidates by merit, contradicting Amin's claims. El Adel also criticized the lack of a public call for applications and clear selection criteria, noting that other students had not received similar opportunities in recent years.

mr.headline: Mauritanian party denounces dialogue committee selection
mr.dek: Al-Messar party criticizes unilateral decision-making process for representatives in national dialogue supervision commission.
paragraphs: The Party for Centre Action and Progress (Al-Messar) in Mauritania has expressed surprise and reservations regarding the selection of representatives for the majority parties' coordination committee overseeing the national dialogue. The party stated it was not consulted on the chosen method for selecting eight individuals, many of whom are party leaders, for the supervision commission.

Al-Messar communicated its objections in a letter to the Coordination of Majority Parties, calling for a review of the "unilateral methodology and adopted criteria" to ensure more inclusive and equitable representation. The party noted that the names were finalized and sent to the dialogue coordinator without addressing its concerns or demands.

The Front for Citizenship and Justice (JAM) also suspended relations with the Coordination of Majority Parties, citing the exclusion of its request to join the supervision commission and claiming some appointees hinder dialogue. Al-Messar urged the adoption of clear, participatory decision-making mechanisms within the coordination to strengthen partnership and serve national interests.

mu.headline: Mauritius cancels Cambridge exams over security concerns
mu.dek: Students face uncertainty as government announces reliance on assessed grades following exam cancellations.
paragraphs: Cambridge exams scheduled for October 13 in Mauritius were cancelled due to recent tensions, leaving students uncertain about their evaluations. Suttyhudeo Tengur stated on Facebook that while student safety was paramount, their academic future requires equal determination. The government announced that "assessed grades" would be used for these candidates, assuring no one would be penalised.

Tengur questioned the official announcement, asking why this solution was presented as final before Cambridge's agreement and demanding the Ministry of Education release Cambridge Assessment International Education's written response. He warned that statistical methods might not reflect individual potential, and small discrepancies could alter university paths. Tengur urged the ministry and the Mauritius Examinations Syndicate to clarify evaluation methods, eligibility, and review procedures.

He also called for a dedicated contact person, clear deadlines, and pedagogical and psychological support. Tengur suggested financial aid if a new session becomes necessary for some candidates. He insisted Cambridge must justify its methods and Mauritian authorities must firmly defend students' interests, ensuring no student faces avoidable academic penalties due to the crisis.

mu.headline: Mauritius M4 highway environmental report due in November
mu.dek: The 30-kilometer M4 highway project's environmental impact assessment will be made public after review.
paragraphs: The M4 highway project, a planned 30-kilometer dual carriageway linking northern and eastern rural regions, was discussed in parliament on October 20. Member of Parliament Joanna Bérenger questioned Minister of National Infrastructure Ajay Gunness about public consultation outcomes and financing terms, including interest rates.

Minister Gunness stated that the environmental impact assessment report, submitted on April 24, 2026, is being revised to include feedback from three public consultations attended by 242 people. The amended report will be submitted to the Ministry of Environment in November 2026 and then released publicly. A $432 million credit line from Exim Bank of India covers the project, with a variable interest rate of approximately 5.87% at signing on July 22, 2026.

The loan has a 15-year term with a five-year capital repayment deferral, though the M4's specific repayment schedule awaits a dedicated credit agreement. Minister Gunness also confirmed that 25% of works and supplies will be reserved for Mauritian businesses, including SMEs and local suppliers.

mz.headline: Mozambique prison service on high alert for Mondlane trial
mz.dek: The state is preparing for unrest ahead of Venâncio Mondlane's trial, despite his claims he will not incite supporters.
paragraphs: Mozambique’s prison service, SERNAP, is escalating to its highest combat readiness level across all facilities starting November 16, the day before Venâncio Mondlane's trial begins. This heightened security measure is being implemented because the trial is treated as a potential national security crisis. SERNAP is redeploying guards from administrative roles, reinforcing external patrols, and coordinating with police and military forces, particularly in prisons that experienced incursions and escapes during the 2024 unrest.

Despite the state's preparations for potential public unrest, Mondlane stated in an October 18 interview that he would not call his supporters to the streets if convicted. The Council of State suspended Mondlane’s immunity on June 10 to allow the criminal case to proceed at the Supreme Court, a decision Mondlane contests as null. Amnesty International reported reckless force and mass arrests during the post-election crackdown in April 2025, with the civil society platform DECIDE counting around 315 deaths between October 2024 and January 2025.

The directive for increased prison security emphasizes proportionality and respect for human rights, though past actions by security forces have been criticized. Frelimo, the ruling party, stands to gain from the weakening of its prominent opponent, making the court's independence a significant factor in the proceedings.

The party's National Council made the decision in Maputo, citing serious disciplinary offences under article 15(f) of its statutes. Renamo spokesman Marcial Macome stated that a disciplinary process preceded the expulsion.

Muchanga, who has publicly called for leader Ossufo Momade's resignation over the past year, was a recognisable critic. This move may make meetings easier for Ossufo Momade but weakens Renamo's ability to unite its factions. The party lost voters in 2024 and needs to win them back. Muchanga's public profile gave a recognisable face to internal grievances, which remain unanswered by his removal.

mz.headline: BNI sues former minister over business debt
mz.dek: Banco Nacional de Investimento seeks to recover funds lent to Topa Internacional, Lda., owned by ex-minister Ragendra Berta de Sousa.
paragraphs: The Banco Nacional de Investimento (BNI) is pursuing legal action against former Minister of Industry and Commerce, Ragendra Berta de Sousa, for an unpaid business loan. The debt was incurred by his company, Topa Internacional, Lda., based in Machava, Maputo province. A court notice from the Commercial Section of the Maputo City Judicial Court has been published, initiating a 20-day public announcement period for unknown creditors.

The court is calling on creditors of Topa Internacional, Lda., Ragendra Berta de Sousa, and Seouk-Kyu Chun to come forward within 10 days to claim the executive action case files. The BNI is the plaintiff in this case, seeking payment of a certain amount. The loan was specifically for financing the acquisition of movable goods, described as flexible packaging industry equipment.

Ragendra de Sousa led the sector between 2017 and 2020. During his tenure, he famously promised to resign if the Companhia de Búzi, located in Sofala province, was not rehabilitated, a commitment made in April 2018. The factory remains abandoned to date. The exact debt amount and the year of the loan are not disclosed in the public announcement.

Deputy board chairperson Stephanie de Klerk stated that this temporary reopening does not signal a return to normal operations or the resumption of buying cattle from farmers. While domestic sales will generate some revenue, Meatco warned that local market prices cannot replace the higher margins earned from international markets, leaving the company under continued financial pressure.

The disruption has affected Meatco's cash flow, prompting emergency cost-containment measures. The company is exploring alternative sales channels with domestic retailers and hospitality businesses. A broader resumption of slaughtering and livestock procurement depends on further directives from the Directorate of Veterinary Services, with no timeline provided for restoring normal operations.

na.headline: Namibia clears table grape exports to China
na.dek: China's zero-tariff policy offers Namibian producers a pricing advantage for grapes and wild aquatic products.
paragraphs: Namibia has approved table grape exports to China, opening a new market under the countries' agricultural cooperation agreement. Chinese ambassador Zhao Weiping announced the approval, which also covers wild aquatic products, at a seminar in Windhoek. This move provides Namibian grape exporters with a pricing advantage due to China's zero-tariff policy for African countries.

Exporters must demonstrate consistent quality and reliable supply to scale up volumes in the Chinese market. The agreement diversifies Namibia's export base beyond single commodities, creating additional revenue streams. Minister Inge Zaamwani stated Namibia is shifting towards irrigation and climate-smart farming, with four areas identified for agricultural development cooperation with China.

This cooperation follows President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah’s July 2026 visit to China, which focused on food security and farming technology. The focus on value addition matters because fresh grape exports capture less value than processed products, and Namibia has limited agro-processing capacity. Key for investors will be the borehole project's water delivery and Namibian exporters' ability to meet Chinese phytosanitary requirements.

na.headline: Namibian microlender skipped loan checks
na.dek: The financial regulator found a microlender failed to verify borrower repayment ability before issuing loans.
paragraphs: Namibia’s financial regulator, Namfisa, discovered a microlender issued loans without the required documents to prove borrowers could afford repayments. The finding occurred during an on-site inspection in the second quarter of 2026. Namfisa did not disclose the number of loans affected or the specific lender.

The inspection revealed instances of non-compliance, including granting loans without mandatory supporting documentation for affordability assessments. The microlending industry’s total loan book grew by 27% quarter on quarter to N$9.3 billion by the end of June 2026. Namfisa stated further action could be considered after final findings are available.

Namibian microlenders dominate high-risk categories, with 43 of 52 non-bank financial institutions in Stage 5 (near insolvency) being microlenders. Another 37 of 38 institutions in Stage 4 (serious doubts about future) were also microlenders. An administrative penalty against one microlender is under consideration.

na.headline: Namibia Securities Exchange sets listing rules
na.dek: Companies must use approved sponsors and submit documentation for exchange approval before public announcements.
paragraphs: Firms aiming to list on the Namibia Securities Exchange (NSX) must first engage an approved Namibian sponsor. This sponsor will guide the company through the formal application process, including identifying and preparing the necessary documentation for submission. The NSX reviews these documents to ensure they are complete and satisfactory before an application can proceed.

Following the review, the application is presented to the listing committee for consideration. If the committee approves, the application moves to the NSX board for final approval for a primary listing. Companies are restricted from making public announcements about their listing intentions until final approval is granted by the executive committee.

A company can announce it has submitted an application once the NSX has received a complete submission, but this does not guarantee approval. The time required for a listing varies based on the application's complexity and the process of meeting all requirements and obtaining necessary approvals.

na.headline: Nanso Zambezi seeks government support for student welfare
na.dek: The Namibia National Students Organisation regional chapter faces challenges implementing congress resolutions due to lack of government assistance.
paragraphs: The Namibia National Students Organisation (NANSO) in the Zambezi Region stated on Wednesday that a lack of government support hinders its work addressing student concerns. Regional representatives voiced these issues during a panel discussion hosted by the ministry of information and communication technology’s Zambezi Regional Office.

NANSO representatives cited difficulties in securing transport and logistical aid from government offices, emphasizing the need for stronger collaboration. The organisation had sought N$445 000 for its 19th National Students Congress in August, which was affected by government funding cuts. Resolutions from the congress called for improved student welfare and sustained government support for recognised student bodies.

Shazzy Liswaniso, overseeing gender affairs, said collaboration should extend beyond meetings to regular communication and follow-ups. Munisola Munisola, the regional finance officer, noted that fundraising plans for next year require government and stakeholder support, including logistical assistance for meetings.

ne.headline: Niger justice minister launches legal document training
ne.dek: Minister Alio Daouda initiated a campaign to improve the creation of legal execution documents by judicial staff.
paragraphs: Niger's Minister of Justice, Alio Daouda, officially launched a campaign in Niamey on October 23, 2026, to train judicial personnel on the proper procedures for creating and issuing legal execution documents. This initiative stems from findings during a February 16 to July 10, 2026, field mission which revealed that judicial services were hindered by the inconsistent or absent establishment of these critical documents.

The minister explained that the campaign addresses a lack of knowledge regarding best practices, which have been neglected. Execution documents, defined as certified extracts from court minutes signed by clerks, are essential for enforcing final criminal decisions, including imprisonment and the collection of fines. They also provide a record of an individual's criminal history through judicial records.

The Director General of Legal Affairs and Seals, Elhj Basshir Mai Moussa, further clarified that these documents are vital for initiating the recovery of penalties and fines, and for applying sanctions. The campaign aims to ensure the reliable maintenance of judicial records and to streamline the payment of fines to the state.

ne.headline: Niger launches campaign against female cancers
ne.dek: Around 395 cases of female cancers were diagnosed in Niger in 2025, prompting a new awareness drive.
paragraphs: Niger launched its "Octobre Rose" campaign to raise awareness about female cancers, with approximately 395 cases diagnosed in 2025. The initiative aims to encourage women to undergo screenings for breast and cervical cancers.

Dr. Ramatoulaye Diop Cissé, Director General of the Afoua clinic, explained that a special space is available for patients and doctors to discuss concerns openly, away from clinical pressure. The clinic has also organized a three-day screening caravan in Harkanassou and an art exhibition on October 24th.

For six years, free screenings for precancerous cervical lesions and breast cancer have been offered, alongside training on self-examination. The campaign utilizes various channels, including media support and involvement from artists and different social groups, to spread its message.

ne.headline: Algeria's parliament to vote on Niger troop deployment
ne.dek: Algerian lawmakers will convene on Sunday, October 25, to consider sending troops to Niger.
paragraphs: Algerian lawmakers are being urgently summoned to parliament on Sunday, October 25, to potentially approve the deployment of troops to Niger. This move follows a recent military cooperation agreement signed between the two nations on October 21, aimed at strengthening security ties.

The Algerian Minister of Defense met with his Nigerien counterpart in Algiers on October 21, signing a military protocol to enhance cooperation. This agreement comes two months after a mutiny in Niger, with Algiers providing military support to the current Niamey government led by Abdourahamane Tiani.

The Algerian constitution requires parliamentary approval for troop deployments abroad. The specific agenda for the October 25 session has not been officially stated, but sources suggest it concerns validating the dispatch of soldiers to Niger.

ne.headline: two European women freed in Libya after Niger kidnapping
ne.dek: Austrian and Swiss nationals were held for over a year and a half before their release.
paragraphs: An Austrian and a Swiss woman kidnapped in Niger more than a year and a half ago have been freed and are in Libya, Bern and Vienna announced Thursday. 69-year-old Swiss national Claudia Abbt and 76-year-old Eva Gretzmacher arrived in the eastern city of Benghazi where they received medical treatment. Their release follows an intervention by Libyan military commander Khalifa Haftar. No group has publicly claimed responsibility for the abductions.

Both women were living in Agadez in northern Niger when they were captured and had been involved in education and development initiatives. They were met in Benghazi by teams from their respective countries. The Swiss government told the BBC that the freed national was on her way back to Switzerland. Gretzmacher was taken on 11 January 2025, while Abbt was captured in April last year.

Many experts and Nigerien media outlets have suggested that the Islamic State in the Sahel jihadist group, or its affiliated groups, could be responsible. Looking tired, they appeared in a broadcast by an eastern-based television channel Al-Masar thanking Haftar and his son, Saddam, for securing their freedom.
